content.text:
Notable differences found so far:
- 351.503(c)(4): proposed "consistent with an agency's' appropriate issuance(s)" → final "agency's appropriate issuance(s)" (typo fix).
- 351.504(a)(1)-(3): proposed "should be identified" → final "must be identified" — substantive-ish (mandatory). Q11 item.
- 351.505(b)(2): proposed "covered by Sec. 351.503(b)" → final "Sec. 351.504(b)" — a cross-reference to a different section. Per instructions, "a change in which section... a cross-reference points to is not citation format" — so this counts as a real difference! Great Q11 item (and it's the one that matters for Q3).
- 351.505(c)(2): proposed "under paragraphs (a) and (b)" → final "under paragraph (a) and paragraph (b)" (wording only).
- 351.506(c)(1): proposed "their performance credit... and their service computation dates" → final "the employee's performance credit ... the employee's service computation date" (wording). Also (c)(1) "if applicable" same.
- 351.506(d): proposed "has no right to review..." → final adds "under this section" and "This paragraph does not limit any right of access available under another statute or regulation." Substantive addition. Q11 item.
- 351.507(b): proposed "retained under any of this paragraph (b)" → final "under any of these provisions" (wording).
- 351.503(d): proposed "pattern D system" → final "pattern D system authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521"; and (e)(2) final adds "as authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521" — substantive clarifications.
- 351.503(b)(3): proposed "equivalent ratings of record" → final "equivalent to ratings of record" (wording).
- 351.202(d) differences as noted.
- 351.203: proposed "Rating of record... (as specified in Sec. 430.208(d))" → final 430.208(e); citation.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

- 351.605: proposed had notification content in the last sentence of (b); final moves to separate (c) and expands; substantive but likely part of "clarifying" item 5.

Also (b)(2) proposed lacks period and parentheses; final same content. Also 351.701(c)(2): proposed "reduction-in-force notices" vs final "reduction in force notices" (wording).
- 351.701(d)... same.
- 351.702(a)(4): continue reading.

Also note proposed subpart G heading "Subpart G--Assignment Rights" vs final "Subpart G--Assignment Rights" (final didn't include heading change instruction? Final had instruction 33 revise 351.701; no heading instruction because current heading is already Assignment Rights).

content.text:
More differences:
- 351.702(a)(4)(v): the proposed rule had NO (v) — the "no assessment required if same position within 5 years and Level 3+" exception is NEW in the final. Big substantive Q11 item! Final adds (v). Was it acknowledged in the digest? Summary item 13 says "Requires skills-based assessments ... (unless the employee held the same or substantially similar position within five years of the RIF and achieved a rating of Level 3...)" — so the summary acknowledges the exception generally, but the "differences from proposal" list (items 1-6) does not mention it. Q11 isn't about acknowledgment though — Q11 just asks for real differences. Good.
- 351.702(a)(4)(iv): proposed had subparagraphs (A)/(B); final restructured into prose with "(1) ... and (2) ...". Format change (counts? It's structural/format — probably not substantive; the substance same). Also (iii) wording: proposed "Does not solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination" → final "Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment." Same substance.
- 351.802(a)(2): proposed "veteran status" → final "veterans' preference subgroup"; also (a)(3) proposed "A link to part 351 of this chapter and access to the agency's records" → final "A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency's records". Also final amended the introductory text of (a) (adding "Except as otherwise provided in this part") — proposed didn't. Good Q11 items.

Also note final 351.802(a)(6) — that's in the appeals rule, not this one.

Now, what about 351.202(d) more: proposed (d)(3) "may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part" → final (d)(3) more detailed + (d)(4) requiring notice. Substantive (acknowledged in item 4).

Also final 351.203 adds "Restoration protected employee" (not in proposal) — Q11 item.

Also final 351.203 "Initial probationary period" — same. "Competing employee" same. "Furlough" difference: final removed the clause; acknowledged (item 5) but Q11 doesn't care.

Also 351.505(b)(2) cross-ref: 351.503(b) → 351.504(b) — big Q11 item.

Also 351.502: "date the agency issues" → "date the employee receives" (4 places) — Q11 item.

Also 351.505(c)(2) fine.

Also 351.503(f)(1): identical in both (modal rating as defined in 351.203). So no proposed/final diff there; but the cross-reference to 351.203's modal rating survives in both. So is "modal rating" defined in 351.203? Not printed in either doc. Hmm. So Q4(e) answer: the rule refers to the modal rating "as defined in Sec. 351.203," but neither document prints that definition, so I can't state it from the FR; the preamble says it uses "the modal rating concept ... as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)" — i.e., the summary level most frequently assigned (mode) in the applicable pattern. Under the assumption of a five-level pattern, the modal rating would be whichever level is most common; not determinable per employee. Hmm, but the question asks "What performance credit does he get?" Expected answer likely: the credit for the modal rating (mode) of the pattern — and since we can't know, we say credit based on the modal rating; note definition isn't printed. Actually maybe the intended answer is that this is a drafting gap: the final rule cross-references a definition in 351.203 that the rule itself does not add or print. Hmm — but maybe old 351.203 does define modal rating (pre-existing), in which case it stays. Since old 351.203 wasn't fully printed, we can't verify. I'll present: the rule directs use of the modal rating as defined in 351.203; the FR documents don't print that definition, so its precise content can't be verified here; if the definition is the one the preamble describes (the modal rating concept formerly in 351.504(c)(1)), credit = 3 × points for that level? Wait — for an employee with NO ratings, "performance credit must be based on the modal rating," singular — so presumably credit = value of modal rating × 3 (three-year equivalent), or just the value? Old rule 351.504(c)(1): "the performance credit of an employee who has not received a rating of record ... will be based on the modal rating for the pattern..." Under old system, credit was expressed in years; modal rating's value times 3? Hmm.

I'll say: credit is the modal rating's point value; most defensible reading is that the employee receives the value of the modal rating repeated for each of the three missing years (i.e., 3 × the modal level's points), consistent with 351.503(f)(3)'s approach for one rating (points × 3). And flag uncertainty since 351.203's modal-rating definition isn't printed. Also note the preamble describes it as carrying forward the "modal rating concept" from former 351.504(c)(1).

OK. Time is limited. Let me now handle Q13 and remaining items. For Q13 I need preamble statements in the main final rule that conflict with its own regulatory text. Candidates found so far:
(1) Digest item 3 (91 FR 49179): "an agency must submit a description of the competitive area and provide, for OPM review, a written explanation of the bona fide organizational basis" vs 351.402(c): "shall submit... to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force." Different (review vs approval). Page 49179 vs 49220.
(2) Preamble 2536-2537: "this rule does not change ... the notice requirements in Sec. 351.802, except to conform their provisions to other changes" vs text amending 351.802(a)(2),(3) adding veterans' preference subgroup and link. Pages 49198 vs 49226. Weak-ish but real.
(3) Example 3 table (2689-2698): Carl's SCD listed as 01/01/2010 in second table though 01/01/2022 in first — that's an internal inconsistency but not preamble vs text.
(4) 351.503(f)(1) "modal rating as defined in Sec. 351.203" vs preamble 2470-2472 "uses the modal rating concept ... as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)" — cross-reference mismatch: preamble says the concept is found in 351.504(c)(1), text says defined in 351.203. Good Q13 candidate (page 49198 vs 49221).
(5) 351.504(b) text vs preamble? Need to check preamble on veterans' preference/retired members — maybe the preamble says something different about retired members. Let's search.
(6) 351.701(b)(1) requires "same tenure group" for assignment rights; preamble elsewhere might say "same tenure subgroup" or "lower retention standing" only. Check subpart G preamble.
(7) 351.507(a) says standing determined as of date employee "receives" notice; preamble 2814-2816 says same. Fine.
(8) 351.202(d): preamble digest says employees serving "temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less" excluded — text (d)(1)(i) excepted service temp/time-limited ≤1 year; competitive service only temporary appointment of 1 year or less (subpart D). Preamble item 2 says "temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less" generally (both services). Also preamble summary item 2 says "Employees serving initial probationary periods, trial periods..." Fine.
(9) Preamble 2276-2278: "The competitive service tenure group will consist of all competitive service employees ... who are not (as of the date of the RIF notice) serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR part 316" — but the text 351.502(a)(3) says "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316" (not time-limited, not subpart C). Mismatch: preamble includes "time-limited" appointments and refers to all of part 316; text says only temporary appointment under subpart D. That's a Q13 candidate (page 49196 vs 49220). Also preamble 2287-2290: "Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other competitive service employee who ... is not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less" — mentions "term" appointments while text says "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" (no term). Good candidate.
(10) Preamble 2499-2501 (current rules) — not about this rule.
(11) 351.701(a): "minimally satisfactory (Level 2)"; preamble?
(12) Check the Subpart G preamble and Subpart H preamble and Part 330 section for mismatches.

Let me read preamble Subpart F & G (2835-3145) — needed for Q6(e) and Q9 (exceptions/stacking) and Q13.

  2835  E. Part 351, Subpart F: Furloughs, Abolishment of Competitive Area, 
  2836  USERRA Rights, and Exceptions
  2837  
  2838      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.601 for consistency with how retention 
  2839  standing is to be calculated under Subpart E of part 351. OPM is also 
  2840  modifying Sec.  351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an 
  2841  employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a 
  2842  competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level. 
  2843  OPM did not receive significant adverse comments on these provisions 
  2844  and is finalizing them.
  2845  1. RIF Furloughs
  2846      In the proposed rule, OPM proposed to modify its regulations in 
  2847  Sec.  351.604 regarding furloughs of more than 30 consecutive calendar 
  2848  days (or more than 22 workdays if done on a discontinuous basis over a 
  2849  period not exceeding 1 year) to remove the requirement that agencies 
  2850  furlough employees based on retention standing and recall employees to 
  2851  duty from furlough based on retention standing.
  2852      Commenter 0687 opposed these changes, contending that they had ``no 
  2853  obvious use case and could create mechanisms for abuse.'' Commenter 
  2854  0687 noted that agencies typically do not engage in unpaid furloughs of 
  2855  any length, whether greater or less than 30 days, and that OPM's 
  2856  proposed revision would create risks that agencies could use long 
  2857  furloughs to circumvent normal RIF procedures. Commenter 0687 therefore 
  2858  contended that the risks of this new provision outweigh the benefits. 
  2859  Commenter 0117 similarly expressed concern that agencies could use 
  2860  long-term unpaid furloughs to avoid following retention order 
  2861  requirements. OPM agrees that its proposed changes to Sec.  351.604 
  2862  warrant further consideration and has chosen not to finalize them.
  2863  2. Abolishment of a Competitive Area
  2864      In this rule, OPM is renaming Sec.  351.605 as Abolishment of a 
  2865  competitive area to more accurately describe its purpose. The revised 
  2866  section explains that the appropriate use of this provision is when an 
  2867  agency is abolishing all positions (including the positions of 
  2868  employees otherwise excluded from RIF competition under Sec.  
  2869  351.202(d)) in a competitive area within 180 days. It further explains 
  2870  that, because all positions in the competitive area will be eliminated, 
  2871  an agency is not required to release competing employees in order of 
  2872  retention standing.
  2873      As the D.C. Circuit explained in upholding an earlier version of 
  2874  this provision, when all employees in a competitive area will be 
  2875  released within a relatively short time, ``it is certainly reasonable 
  2876  to conclude that it would be a waste of resources for an agency to be 
  2877  forced to perform detailed seniority and performance calculations 
  2878  solely to construct a rank ordering of employees' retention rights when 
  2879  those rights are of such little value.'' AFGE v. OPM, 821 F.2d at 766 
  2880  n. 4. Thus, OPM was ``within its authority to conclude that under those 
  2881  limited circumstances, no effect is `due.' '' Id. With performance now 
  2882  the main consideration governing RIF retention, the same considerations 
  2883  apply: it does not make sense to require agencies to perform detailed 
  2884  seniority and performance calculations to construct a rank ordering of 
  2885  employees that will have no substantive effect on their retention 
  2886  rights.
  2887      In this final rule, OPM is making minor wording and ordering 
  2888  changes to this provision. Section 351.605(c) provides that any 
  2889  competing employee released under this provision must be provided a 
  2890  specific written notice in accordance with Sec.  351.801, Notice 
  2891  period. The notice must include the following: the action being taken 
  2892  and its effective date; the competitive area being abolished; a link to 
  2893  5 CFR part 351 and access to the agency's records pertinent to the RIF 
  2894  being run to abolish the competitive area; information on reemployment 
  2895  rights; the employee's appeal rights; and a statement that, because all 
  2896  positions in the competitive area are being abolished pursuant to 5 CFR 
  2897  351.605, the employee was not ranked relative to other competing 
  2898  employees in the reduction in force. The notice is not required to 
  2899  include the information described in Sec.  351.802(a)(2) or (a)(4).
  2900      Section 351.605(d), Retention register not required, explains that 
  2901  an agency is not required to rank competing employees in the abolished 
  2902  competitive area, and must not apply the assignment right provisions in 
  2903  subpart G, because
  2904  
  2905  [[Page 49203]]
  2906  
  2907  no positions in the competitive area will remain.
  2908      Commenter 0683 suggested that OPM review and approve any 
  2909  competitive area abolishment due to the potential that agencies could 
  2910  use this provision alongside the new competitive area definition to 
  2911  evade the need to build a retention register and provide assignment 
  2912  rights. OPM believes that these concerns are adequately addressed by 
  2913  the requirement in Sec.  351.402(c) that OPM approve new or 
  2914  substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less 
  2915  than 90 days prior to the issuance of RIF notices; the requirement in 
  2916  Sec.  351.204 that agencies must administer and apply the regulations 
  2917  consistent with all applicable laws, including the Merit System 
  2918  Principles in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b); the requirement that the competitive 
  2919  area be disclosed to the employee in the RIF notice; and the 
  2920  availability of RIF appeal rights in Subpart I of 5 CFR part 351.
  2921      Commenter 0683 also asked that OPM clarify that the abolishment of 
  2922  a competitive area under Section 351.605 does not diminish or supersede 
  2923  the statutory placement rights of career SES members under 5 U.S.C. 
  2924  3594-3595. OPM confirms that these revisions are not intended to 
  2925  diminish or supersede career SES placement rights in a RIF. However, 
  2926  OPM believes that 5 CFR 359.602(b) is clear enough on this point that 
  2927  no change to the regulatory text in 5 CFR part 351 is required.
  2928  3. USERRA Rights
  2929      In the proposed rule, OPM proposed to modify Sec.  351.606(a), 
  2930  which addresses mandatory RIF exceptions for employees who have been 
  2931  restored or reemployed following uniformed service and who remain 
  2932  entitled to post-reemployment retention protection under Sec.  
  2933  353.209(b) for either 6 months or 1 year. These retention rights are 
  2934  provided under USERRA.
  2935      Commenter 0686, a Federal agency, requested that OPM clarify the 
  2936  proposed modifications to Sec.  351.606, and particularly its 
  2937  interaction with Sec.  351.605, which revises the procedures to be 
  2938  followed when a competitive area is abolished. Several other commenters 
  2939  (0076, 0121, 0455, 0550, 0597) argued that the proposed rule could be 
  2940  read as undermining USERRA rights, including where an employee 
  2941  performing uniformed service or recently reemployed after uniformed 
  2942  service lacks recent civilian performance ratings.
  2943      OPM agrees that clarification is appropriate. Accordingly, OPM in 
  2944  this final rule is making explicit how USERRA restoration and retention 
  2945  protections operate when an employee is affected by a RIF.
  2946      First, OPM is adding a definition of ``Restoration protected 
  2947  employee'' in Sec.  351.203. For purposes of part 351, a restoration 
  2948  protected employee is a competing employee who has been restored or 
  2949  reemployed following uniformed service and who, as of the date the 
  2950  employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, remains within 
  2951  the 6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period described in 
  2952  Sec.  353.209(b). Those protection periods implement 38 U.S.C. 4316(c), 
  2953  which provides that a person reemployed under USERRA may not be 
  2954  discharged from employment, except for cause, for 1 year after 
  2955  reemployment if the period of uniformed service was more than 180 days, 
  2956  or for 180 days after reemployment if the period of service was more 
  2957  than 30 days but less than 181 days.
  2958      Second, OPM is revising Sec.  351.606 to clarify that agencies must 
  2959  apply USERRA retention protections and restoration rights as a 
  2960  mandatory exception to the ordinary RIF order of release. The agency 
  2961  must first determine the employee's ordinary retention standing under 
  2962  subpart E. The agency must then apply the mandatory exception in Sec.  
  2963  351.606(a). During the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period, 
  2964  the agency may not release a restoration protected employee from the 
  2965  competitive level if another competing employee may be released 
  2966  instead.
  2967      Third, OPM is clarifying how the mandatory exception applies when 
  2968  an agency abolishes all positions in a competitive area under Sec.  
  2969  351.605. When an entire competitive area is abolished pursuant to Sec.  
  2970  351.605, the agency may not separate the restoration protected employee 
  2971  by RIF during the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period. 
  2972  Instead, the employee must be assigned by the agency to a different 
  2973  position of like seniority, status, and pay for which the employee is 
  2974  qualified, consistent with 5 CFR part 353.
  2975      Fourth, OPM is revising Sec.  353.209(a) to conform part 353 to 
  2976  these part 351 clarifications. Section 353.209(a) already provides that 
  2977  an employee performing duty with the uniformed services may not be 
  2978  demoted or separated, other than military separation, except for cause; 
  2979  that RIF is not ``for cause'' under that subpart; that the employee is 
  2980  not a competing employee under part 351; and that, if the employee's 
  2981  position is abolished during the absence, the agency must reassign the 
  2982  employee to another position of like status and pay. OPM is clarifying 
  2983  that this reassignment obligation applies when the employee's position 
  2984  is abolished in a RIF, including when all positions in the employee's 
  2985  competitive area are abolished under Sec.  351.605.
  2986      Fifth, OPM is clarifying the relationship between part 351, part 
  2987  353, and 38 U.S.C. 4314 when the employing agency can no longer place 
  2988  the employee. If the employee's function has been transferred to 
  2989  another agency, the employee's rights are governed by the transfer and 
  2990  restoration provisions in 5 CFR part 353. If the employing agency no 
  2991  longer exists and its functions have not been transferred, or if it is 
  2992  impossible or unreasonable for the agency to reassign the restoration 
  2993  protected employee, OPM will offer placement assistance elsewhere in 
  2994  the executive branch to the employee pursuant to 5 CFR 353.110.
  2995      These revisions also address concerns that employees performing 
  2996  uniformed service, or recently returned from uniformed service, may 
  2997  lack recent civilian ratings of record. This rule's missing-rating 
  2998  provisions continue to address how ordinary performance credit is 
  2999  calculated for competing employees who do not have three ratings of 
  3000  record, including use of the modal rating for employees with no ratings 
  3001  during the relevant four-year period and proxy rules for employees with 
  3002  one or two ratings. But for a restoration-protected employee within the 
  3003  6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period, the mandatory 
  3004  exception in Sec.  351.606(a) operates independently of the employee's 
  3005  ordinary retention standing. Thus, the employee is not penalized for 
  3006  lacking recent civilian ratings during the protected period; the agency 
  3007  must honor the USERRA retention protection before releasing the 
  3008  employee by RIF.
  3009      In addition, this rule preserves credit for uniformed service in 
  3010  calculating length of service for RIF purposes. Section 351.505(b)(1) 
  3011  provides that all active duty in a uniformed service, as defined in 5 
  3012  U.S.C. 2101(3), is creditable for purposes of part 351, except as 
  3013  otherwise provided in that section. The service computation date 
  3014  includes all actual creditable service under Sec.  351.505(a) and (b).
  3015  4. Exceptions
  3016      OPM is modifying and clarifying current Sec.  351.607, relabeling 
  3017  this section as Discretionary continuing exceptions to harmonize this 
  3018  section with other provisions in this chapter for which agency use is 
  3019  optional. OPM is also modifying and clarifying Sec.  351.608, renaming 
  3020  this section Discretionary
  3021  
  3022  [[Page 49204]]
  3023  
  3024  temporary exceptions. OPM is also creating new flexibilities for an 
  3025  agency to retain an employee past the effective date of a RIF due to a 
  3026  government obligation. Section 351.608(c) now includes additional 
  3027  examples of situations in which the exception may be used, such as when 
  3028  an employee, or spouse of an employee, is pregnant on the effective 
  3029  date of a RIF or an employee has not used all available paid parental 
  3030  leave to care for a recently born child or a child recently placed with 
  3031  the employee for adoption purposes.
  3032      Paragraph (d) of Sec.  351.608 expands the existing exception to 
  3033  allow employees with medical conditions or other circumstances that 
  3034  would qualify for use of sick leave to use other appropriate leave 
  3035  (paid or unpaid) or other paid time off in addition to sick leave, 
  3036  subject to a 90-day cap and provided that the leave is used 
  3037  continuously. Section 351.608(e) labels this provision ``annual leave'' 
  3038  to make clear the type of leave appropriate for an exception under this 
  3039  paragraph, which has been expanded to include not only employees 
  3040  covered by a Federal leave system under an authority other than 5 
  3041  U.S.C. chapter 63 but also employees covered by a retirement law not 
  3042  referenced in Sec.  351.606(b) or a health benefits law other than 5 
  3043  U.S.C. chapter 89. A new Sec.  351.608(f) establishes a temporary 
  3044  exception for military spouses as defined in Sec.  351.203. An agency 
  3045  may retain an eligible military spouse for up to 90 days beyond the 
  3046  effective date of a RIF. OPM did not receive significant adverse 
  3047  comment regarding its proposed changes to sections 351.607 and 351.608 
  3048  and is finalizing them.
  3049  
  3050  F. Part 351, Subpart G: Assignment Rights
  3051  
  3052      OPM is revising Sec.  351.701(a) to replace tenure groups I and II 
  3053  with the competitive service tenure group in conformance with other 
  3054  changes in this rulemaking.
  3055      OPM is consolidating Sec.  351.701(b) and (c), simplifying the 
  3056  method of applying assignment rights. Based on the new method of 
  3057  defining tenure groups and assigning retention standing based on 
  3058  performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, with tenure 
  3059  subgroup and length of service as tiebreakers, subgroups will no longer 
  3060  play a predominant role in determining retention standing, and thus 
  3061  there is no longer a need for the separate concepts of an employee 
  3062  ``bumping'' another employee in a lower subgroup, and ``retreating'' to 
  3063  the position of a lower-ranked employee in the same subgroup. Instead, 
  3064  a released employee will have assignment rights to a position held by 
  3065  another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure 
  3066  group, who is not more than three grades below the position from which 
  3067  the employee was released, and for which the released employee is 
  3068  qualified, pursuant to the criteria set forth in Sec.  351.702 and 
  3069  Sec.  351.703. This reform will significantly simplify the process of 
  3070  applying assignment rights in a RIF, eliminating the need for 
  3071  successive rounds of bumping and retreating between and within 
  3072  different subgroups.
  3073      OPM is eliminating Sec.  351.701(d). With the new method of 
  3074  calculating retention standing implemented in this rulemaking, which 
  3075  emphasizes performance over tenure and length of service, OPM believes 
  3076  that this restriction on employees with a current annual performance 
  3077  rating of record of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held 
  3078  by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary. 
  3079  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment on the removal of this 
  3080  provision.
  3081      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.702(a)(4), pertaining to qualifications 
  3082  for assignment to a new position, to include language clarifying that 
  3083  in determining qualifications for reassignment an agency must use an 
  3084  assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related skills, 
  3085  abilities, knowledge, and competencies; is based on a job analysis; and 
  3086  does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination. 
  3087  Commenter 0687 supported this change, expressing ``appreciat[ion] that 
  3088  OPM has added a mechanism for agencies to utilize assessments to 
  3089  determine qualification for those assignments that is skills-based and 
  3090  consistent with merit principles in selection.''
  3091      On the other hand, Commenter 0685 expressed concern that the use of 
  3092  assessments would ``inject subjectivity into what has traditionally 
  3093  been a more mechanical qualification determination.'' OPM disagrees. 
  3094  The current rule provides that an employee is qualified for a position 
  3095  if the employee ``[h]as the capacity, adaptability, and special skills 
  3096  needed to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position without 
  3097  undue interruption,'' but provides no other guidance for making this 
  3098  determination, other than that an agency may consider ``recency of 
  3099  experience, when appropriate.'' OPM believes that the use of a 
  3100  validated assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related 
  3101  skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies, such as a structured 
  3102  interview, structured resume review, or a work-related exercise, will 
  3103  reduce the subjectivity of making a qualifications determination, 
  3104  requiring that an employee demonstrate their job-related skills in a 
  3105  measured, objective fashion. In so doing, OPM is aligning qualification 
  3106  determinations for assignment in a RIF with otherwise-applicable merit-
  3107  based hiring practices required under E.O. 13932, E.O. 14171, the 
  3108  Chance to Compete Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-188), and the Merit Hiring 
  3109  Plan.\17\
  3110  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3111  
  3112      \17\ Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy & OPM, Merit 
  3113  Hiring Plan (May 29, 2025), https://www.opm.gov/chcoc/latest-memos/merit-hiring-plan.pdf.
  3114  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3115  
  3116      However, OPM recognizes that, in some circumstances, requiring a 
  3117  new assessment may be unnecessary where official records already show 
  3118  that the employee recently and successfully performed the same or 
  3119  substantially equivalent work. Thus, in the Final Rule, OPM is 
  3120  providing that an agency is not required to administer an assessment 
  3121  if, during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a 
  3122  specific RIF notice, the employee occupied the same position, or a 
  3123  position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same 
  3124  duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions 
  3125  of employment, and received a rating of record of Level 3, Fully 
  3126  Successful, or higher, or the equivalent, for performance of those 
  3127  duties. This provision is intended to reduce unnecessary assessments 
  3128  while preserving the requirement that assignment rights be based on the 
  3129  employee's ability to perform the work.
  3130      OPM is modifying current Sec.  351.705 Administrative assignment to 
  3131  eliminate references to optional agency flexibilities to allow 
  3132  employees with lower retention standing to displace an employee with 
  3133  higher standing in the same subgroup under certain circumstances. With 
  3134  the more merit-based and straightforward order of retention implemented 
  3135  in this rulemaking, there is no longer a need for these exceptions.
  3136      OPM is retaining, and renumbering, current Sec.  351.705(c), which 
  3137  provides that agencies may, at their discretion, provide competing 
  3138  employees in the excepted service with assignment rights to other 
  3139  positions under the same appointing authority on the same basis as 
  3140  assignment rights provided to competitive service employees under Sec.  
  3141  351.701.
  3142  
  3143  G. Part 351, Subpart H: Notice Provisions
  3144

content.text:
Excellent — Q6(e) material: preamble 3055-3072 explains bumping/retreating eliminated; 3073-3080 explains eliminating former 351.701(d) (which had restricted Level 2 employees from assignment to positions held by employees with higher ratings). Great: the old HR handbook statement about "a Level 2 employee cannot take a position held by someone with a higher rating" — 2026 documents say that restriction was eliminated (former 351.701(d)). And "bumping vs retreating" concepts are replaced. Good.

Also Q13 candidate: preamble 3098-3099: "The current rule provides ... other than that an agency may consider 'recency of experience, when appropriate.'" Not a rule statement.

Also preamble 2909-2915: "the requirement in Sec. 351.402(c) that OPM approve new or substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less than 90 days prior to the issuance of RIF notices" — consistent with text (approval).

Q13: digest item 3 said "provide, for OPM review, a written explanation" — conflicts with "for approval". Good.

Also preamble Subpart F: "Section 351.605(c) provides that any competing employee released under this provision must be provided a specific written notice in accordance with Sec. 351.801, Notice period." Then lists required contents. Text says notice must include (a)(1),(3),(5),(6) and (b). So preamble summarizes. Does preamble include (b)? unclear. Not a strong mismatch.

Note: preamble 2891-2895 lists notice content including "information on reemployment rights; the employee's appeal rights" — text (a)(5),(6). OK.

Now the Subpart H preamble (3143-3200) for Q9 step 12 and Q13.

  3173  OPM is also updating language in Sec.  351.802(a)(3) by requiring

  3175  and access to the agency's records pertinent to the RIF being run.
  3176      OPM is adopting a clarifying amendment to Sec.  351.805(b) to

  3207  I. Part 330: RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP
  3208  
  3209      OPM is making various changes to 5 CFR part 330 to conform the

  3211  changes made in this rulemaking, most notably the modifications to

content.text:
Q10 answered: On Sept 10, 2026, paragraph (1) contained only the introductory text (no (i) or (ii)), because instruction 11 in the Aug 3 final rule (91 FR 49217) revised only paragraph (1) and thereby deleted (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as an unintended effect. On Sept 15, 2026 the correction (2026-18800, 91 FR 58363) restored them, effective Sept 15, 2026, with good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) and (d)(3), characterizing it as making no substantive change / restoring text in effect before Sept 2.

Q10(c): After the change: (1)(i) — "Received a RIF separation notice ... and has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated." So if Nadia is offered a full-time position with a LOWER representative rate than her present full-time position and declines, she has not declined an offer of a position with a representative rate at least as high as her present position → she remains "displaced." If the offered position had the same representative rate (and same work schedule — full-time; the scenario says full-time), declining it would mean she is not displaced. Note: "same type of work schedule" — she's full-time; offered full-time → same. So with equal representative rate: declining → not displaced.

Careful: the offer language is "at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated" — her present full-time position. Good.

Now Q8: administrative leave rule 2026-21320. Read it — it should amend 5 CFR 351.806 (and 630 subpart N?). Let me get its TOC and regul text.

  1087  M. Duty Status Presumption During RIF Notice Periods (Sec.  351.806)
  1088  
  1089      Comment 0025 urged OPM to preserve the existing duty-status 
  1090  presumption during RIF notice periods, arguing that RIF notices are not 
  1091  disciplinary, that employees perform valuable transition work during 
  1092  notice periods, that existing authorities already address unusual 
  1093  cases, and that OPM has not identified a gap warranting a RIF-specific 
  1094  administrative-leave authorization.
  1095      The final rule preserves the duty-status presumption with a minor 
  1096  change in terminology. Revised Sec.  351.806(a) provides that ``[u]nder 
  1097  ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during 
  1098  the notice period.'' The change from ``when possible'' to ``under 
  1099  ordinary circumstances'' conforms the RIF regulation to the parallel 
  1100  standard in 5 CFR 752.404(b)(3) governing notice periods for proposed 
  1101  removals and suspensions, and more accurately reflects that the

content.text:
Important for Q1(e): 
- 2026-13715 (91 FR 41521, effective 2026-08-06) amends 5 CFR 351.504: remove "430.208(d)" → "430.208(e)". But wait — at that time, 351.504 was the veterans' preference section? Under pre-2026 part 351, 351.504 was "Veterans' preference" and 430.208(d) references... Hmm, actually pre-2026 351.504(b) referenced 430.208(d)? Possibly 351.504 was "performance credit"? Under old rules, 351.504 was "Performance"? Let me think: pre-2026 part 351: 351.501 Order of retention, 351.502 Tenure, 351.503 Length of service, 351.504 Performance, 351.505 Records, 351.506 Effective date. Yes! Old 351.504 was "Performance" (the extra retention service credit provision) — consistent with 430.208 footnote referencing "additional retention service credit under Sec. 351.504" and "351.504(e)". So 2026-13715 amended old 351.504 (Performance) references. Effective Aug 6, 2026 — but the main rule (effective Sept 2, 2026) revised subpart E wholesale, superseding. So for Q1(e): 2026-13715 amends part 351, but its effective date (Aug 6, 2026) is BEFORE the main rule's effective date (Sept 2, 2026), so it doesn't qualify under "with effect on or after the main rule's effective date." Good — that's a trap.

- 2026-21316 (91 FR 65904, effective 2026-11-18): amends 351.203 definition of "Rating of record" and 351.503(a)(1) (adding summary performance levels in 430.505(a)(6)). Effective Nov 18, 2026 — AFTER main rule effective date; not yet in force today (Nov 14). Qualifies for Q1(e): in force today? No.

- 2026-21320 (91 FR 65924, effective 2026-11-18): revises 351.806. Also not in force today.

Need to check whether any other 2026 final rule amends part 351 with effect on/after Sept 2: e.g., 2026-15654 (Streamlining Probationary and Trial Period Appeals) — does it amend part 351? Its CFR parts? Let me check quickly. Also 2026-15650. Also 2026-18061 (MSPB misconduct). Also 2026-21319 (time-in-grade).

Let me check fr_doc for 2026-15654, 2026-15650, 2026-21319 quickly (CFR affected fields).

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is adopting, substantially as proposed, its proposed rule eliminating the Time-in- Grade (TIG) restriction on advancement to competitive service positions in the General Schedule (GS).     52  appeals. This revision reflects the Office of Personnel Management's 
    53  (OPM's) rescission of the MSPB's jurisdiction to hear these types of 
    54  appeals. The rule retains MSPB's statutory jurisdiction over Foreign 
    55  Service reduction-in-force appeals under 22 U.S.C. 4010a.

    59  pending cases or to newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken 
    60  before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings, and will continue to 
    61  adjudicate such probationary termination appeals, suitability appeals, 
    62  and RIF appeals.

content.text:
Excellent — Q14(iii) material: MSPB rule inconsistency: the DATES and paragraphs at 51997 (lines 130-140) say MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the effective date; but Section III "Effective Date of Amendment" (91 FR 51998) says "MSPB will adjudicate any RIF appeals it receives after September 2, 2026, in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026" — different triggering event (notice issuance vs RIF effective date). That's an internal inconsistency within the Board's rule. Also compare OPM's rule: applies to RIF actions for which the agency issues a specific RIF notice on or after Sept 2 (notice-based). MSPB says "RIF actions were taken before the rule's effective date" (line 136) — "action taken" is a third formulation.

Also: MSPB retains Foreign Service RIF appeals (22 U.S.C. 4010a) — while OPM's 351.901 gives OPM exclusive jurisdiction over "an action taken under this part" — and 351.901(c)(3) preserves matters within MSPB's independent jurisdiction. Could be an inconsistency: OPM's rule says procedures in subpart I are "sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action taken under this part," while MSPB retains Foreign Service RIF appeals (statutory). Not necessarily inconsistent because OPM says "under this part."

Q13 item: preamble at 1548-1553 says OPM is modifying 351.201(a)(2) to remove erosion-of-duties reclassifications "if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF ... and the RIF would take effect within 180 days." But the actual amendment to 351.201(a)(2) doesn't mention erosion of duties at all — the erosion-of-duties change is in 351.202(c)(3), and the text there has no "180 days" element: it bars reclassification between announcement and completion of the RIF where it would adversely affect retention standing. So the preamble describes (a) the wrong paragraph and (b) a 180-day element that the text doesn't contain. Strong Q13 item (page 49190 vs 49218).

Also Q13: preamble 1600-1602 says competitive service tenure group is employees "not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" — matches text (a)(3) except text also excludes "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" — yes matches. But 2276-2278 says "temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR part 316" — mismatch. And 2287-2290 says "temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less" (no subpart). So the preamble is internally inconsistent too; the text (351.502(a)(3)) excludes only temporary appointments under subpart D.

Also preamble 1608-1619 (supervisory probation) — correctly matches (initial probationary period excludes supervisory probation; both → excluded). Good for Q9 step 3 (Ortiz: career tenure, supervisory probation only → included in RIF; not excluded). This confirms Q9 step 3 is noncompliant.

Great. Now Q14(i): read 2349-2500 of 2026-15666.

  2349  C. Subpart I--Appeals
  2350  
  2351      OPM is revising subpart I of part 351 in full. Revised subpart I 
  2352  establishes the procedures governing appeals to OPM by employees who 
  2353  are subject to covered RIF actions. The revised subpart identifies who 
  2354  may appeal, the burden of proof, filing requirements, party 
  2355  submissions, representation rules, adjudication procedures, remedies, 
  2356  sanctions, reconsideration, Director review, and finality.
  2357  1. Section 351.901--Right To Appeal
  2358      Revised Sec.  351.901 establishes the right to appeal a covered 
  2359  reduction-in-force action to OPM, identifies the appellant's burden of 
  2360  proof, and defines the relationship between the OPM RIF appeal process 
  2361  and other remedial forums.
  2362      Paragraph (a) provides that an employee who has been furloughed for 
  2363  more than 30 days, separated, or demoted by a reduction-in-force action 
  2364  taken under part 351 may appeal that action to OPM. This paragraph 
  2365  identifies the covered actions that may be appealed under subpart I and 
  2366  implements the rule's central procedural change: OPM, rather than MSPB, 
  2367  will adjudicate appeals of covered RIF actions, subject to the 
  2368  applicability provision described below.
  2369      Paragraph (b) establishes the employee's burden of proof. The 
  2370  appellant must prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the 
  2371  written appeal was timely and in the required form; that OPM has 
  2372  jurisdiction over the appeal; that the agency failed to comply with an 
  2373  applicable statute or OPM regulation governing reduction-in-force 
  2374  actions under part 351; and that the failure prejudiced the appellant.
  2375      Paragraph (b)(4) defines the prejudice requirement. The appellant 
  2376  must show that the agency's failure to comply with an applicable RIF 
  2377  statute or OPM regulation caused the appellant to be subjected to the 
  2378  appealed action or to lose a materially more favorable outcome under 
  2379  part 351. This standard is intended to distinguish prejudicial errors 
  2380  from technical or immaterial errors. OPM will not grant relief solely 
  2381  because an agency committed a procedural or technical error if the 
  2382  appellant would have been subject to the same action, or would not have 
  2383  received a materially more favorable outcome, had the agency complied 
  2384  with the applicable requirement. Conversely, prejudice may exist where 
  2385  the violation affected the appellant's retention standing, order of 
  2386  release, assignment rights, notice rights, or other RIF determination 
  2387  in a way that materially affected the outcome of the RIF action as 
  2388  applied to the appellant.
  2389      Paragraph (c)(1) provides that the procedures in part 351 are the 
  2390  sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action covered by this 
  2391  subpart. This provision is intended to avoid duplicative or overlapping 
  2392  RIF appeal processes and to channel covered RIF appeals through the OPM 
  2393  procedure established by this final rule. It also promotes consistent 
  2394  application of OPM's governmentwide RIF regulations and avoids parallel 
  2395  adjudication of the same RIF-compliance issues in multiple forums.
  2396      Paragraph (c)(2) provides that a reduction-in-force action taken 
  2397  under part 351, and any matter relating to an appeal of such an action, 
  2398  may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested 
  2399  through grievance arbitration. This provision forecloses negotiated 
  2400  grievance procedures and grievance arbitration as alternative forums 
  2401  for direct RIF-compliance challenges, for the reasons discussed in 
  2402  Section III.I of this preamble.
  2403      At the same time, paragraph (c)(3) makes clear that the OPM RIF 
  2404  appeal process does not displace matters within the independent 
  2405  jurisdiction of other entities. Employees may continue to file 
  2406  complaints, appeals, or other matters that fall within the independent 
  2407  jurisdiction of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, an 
  2408  Inspector General, MSPB, the Department of Labor Veterans' Employment 
  2409  and Training Service, or the Office of Special Counsel. Thus, OPM will 
  2410  adjudicate whether the RIF action complied with applicable RIF statutes 
  2411  and OPM regulations, while collateral statutory claims remain available 
  2412  in the forums Congress or applicable law has designated for those 
  2413  claims.
  2414      Paragraph (c)(4) also provides that a party cannot obtain judicial 
  2415  review of a decision under this subpart. OPM addresses comments 
  2416  concerning judicial review and the CSRA remedial scheme in Section 
  2417  III.G.
  2418      Consistent with the DATES section of this preamble, the appeal 
  2419  process established by revised Sec.  351.901 and subpart I is available 
  2420  for a reduction-in-force action for which the agency issued the 
  2421  employee a specific RIF notice under Sec.  351.802 on or after the 
  2422  effective date of the final rule under RIN 3206-AO86. An appeal of a 
  2423  reduction-in-force action for which the agency issued that notice 
  2424  before that date--including an appeal pending before the MSPB--
  2425  continues to be adjudicated by the MSPB under the procedures applicable 
  2426  when the action was taken. This applicability provision is stated in 
  2427  the preamble, and the final regulatory text accordingly does not 
  2428  include a separate applicability note in Sec.  351.901.
  2429  2. Section 351.902--Procedures for Submitting Appeals
  2430      Revised Sec.  351.902 describes the procedures and timeline an 
  2431  employee must adhere to when submitting an appeal.
  2432      Paragraph (a) requires a party, or the party's authorized 
  2433  representative, to file an initial appeal or request for 
  2434  reconsideration through the electronic filing system identified on 
  2435  OPM's website. Unless a party demonstrates good cause and obtains 
  2436  approval from OPM, OPM will not accept pleadings, evidence, or 
  2437  documents submitted by electronic mail or postal mail. This requirement 
  2438  is intended to promote consistent intake, reliable service, accurate 
  2439  case tracking, and efficient adjudication.
  2440      Commenters 0066, 0272, 0296, 0299, 0304, and others, criticized the 
  2441  requirement that employees use e-filing exclusively, absent a showing 
  2442  of good
  2443  
  2444  [[Page 49249]]
  2445  
  2446  cause. OPM disagrees with these criticisms. The good cause requirement 
  2447  permits nonelectronic filing methods for filers with a bona fide need 
  2448  while furthering OPM's legitimate interest in maintaining a streamlined 
  2449  case intake system that minimizes errors and delays. OPM notes that the 
  2450  e-filing requirement for RIF appeals for which this rule provides is 
  2451  consistent with the National Labor Relations Board's policy for 
  2452  requiring parties to e-file documents absent justification to file in 
  2453  paper format.\31\ Other agencies, including the FLRA and OSC, also have 
  2454  adopted restrictions on electronic filing.\32\ OPM acknowledges 
  2455  Commenter 0553's concern that the e-filing system described in the 
  2456  proposed rule was not operational and available for public inspection 
  2457  at the time the proposed rule was submitted for public comment. 
  2458  However, OPM is confident that it will have an e-filing system in place 
  2459  by this final rule's effective date.

  2461

  2463  permitted under this section, all documents filed in cases before 
  2464  the [National Labor Relations Board] must be filed electronically,'' 
  2465  and requiring paper filers to include ``a statement explaining why 
  2466  the party does not have access to the means for filing 
  2467  electronically or why filing electronically would impose an undue 
  2468  burden'').
  2469      \32\ See, e.g., 5 CFR 2429.24 (``To file documents by personal 
  2470  delivery, you must schedule an appointment at least one business day 
  2471  in advance.''); Office of Special Counsel, File a Complaint, 
  2472  available at https://www.osc.gov/file-complaint/ (last visited June 
  2473  2, 2026) (requesting that parties submit documents electronically 
  2474  because ``OSC is unable to process paper filings'').
  2475  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2476  
  2477      Paragraph (b) establishes a 30-calendar-day deadline for filing an 
  2478  appeal. An employee may submit an appeal within 30 calendar days from 
  2479  the effective date of the RIF action. The appeal is timely if

But hold on: should Brandt also have a right to a position held by Gomez/Hill/Jones if those had lower standing? No.

Also, do released employees' rights extend to positions whose incumbents are also being released? Not applicable here (different levels).

Let me double check Dube's standing vs Gomez: Dube 18 (II) vs Gomez 17 (I). 351.501(c): tie only when same augmented performance credit. 18 ≠ 17 → Dube higher. Yes.

And Chen (18, I) vs Gomez (17): higher. Yes.

Now (b) explain each choice: three lowest by order of release, skipping Farouk due to mandatory exception.

Hmm, but wait: should the agency instead release Farouk and retain someone else? No—prohibited.

Also need to double check Chen's rating exclusion: Sept 30, 2022 rating is outside four-year window (Oct 5, 2022 cutoff). Yes, excluded. So two actual ratings → 351.503(f)(2) proxy: (7+5)/2 = 6 → total 18. Note the proxy value is a whole number here.

Dube: two ratings 5 and 5 → proxy 5 → total 15 +3 = 18.

Estrada: uses Oct 20, 2026 rating (received after notice Oct 5?) — Wait: notices issued Oct 5, 2026; Estrada's Level 5 received Oct 20, 2026 — AFTER the notice date. 351.503(c)(1): ratings received during the 4-year period prior to the date of issuance of RIF notices. A rating received after the notice date is not within the period (the period ends at issuance). So Estrada's Oct 20, 2026 rating CANNOT be used. So Estrada's three most recent (within period): L4 (11/13/2025), L3 (11/14/2024), L4 (11/15/2023) → 5+3+5 = 13; +3 = 16.

Recompute: Estrada 16, not 18. Then ordering: Alvarez 19; Chen 18 (I); Dube 18 (II); Estrada 16 (I); Brandt 13; Farouk 9.
Tie at 18: Chen (I) ahead of Dube (II).
Order: Alvarez 19, Chen 18, Dube 18, Estrada 16, Brandt 13, Farouk 9.
Release three: Farouk (protected → skip), Brandt (13) release #1, Estrada (16) release #2, Dube (18, II) release #3. So released: Brandt, Estrada, Dube.

That fits nicely: the Oct 20 rating (post-notice) is a trap; and Dube's subgroup II loses the tie to Chen.

So (b): released = Brandt, Estrada, Dube. Retained: Alvarez, Chen, Farouk (mandatory exception), and Quinn (excluded).

(c) Assignments:
- Brandt (13, I; 30%+ disabled → 5 grades): lower-standing holders: Ikeda (9) only. Positions within 5 grades: GS-12, 11, 10, 9, 8. So right to GS-9 Ikeda. Must offer GS-9 (only one available). Why not others: Gomez 17, Hill 14, Jones 15 all higher standing than Brandt's 13.
- Estrada (16, I; no disability → 3 grades: GS-12, 11, 10): holders lower than 16: Hill 14, Jones 15, Ikeda 9. Gomez 17 higher → not available. Among Hill (GS-11) and Jones (GS-10), least reduction = GS-11 → must offer Hill's GS-11. GS-9 Ikeda too far (4 grades).
- Dube (18, II → but 18 highest augmented credit among these, so all four holders lower: Gomez 17, Hill 14, Jones 15, Ikeda 9): 3 grades → GS-12, 11, 10. Least reduction = GS-12 Gomez. Must offer Gomez's GS-12.

Great, now offers don't conflict except Brandt GS-9 (Ikeda) and Dube GS-12 and Estrada GS-11. Clean! (d): Separated: Ikeda, Gomez, Hill (the displaced incumbents), since each is qualified only for the position they held and thus has no assignment rights. Also note displaced employees are released from their levels and entitled to RIF procedures/notice; but on these facts they're separated. Quinn stays (not a competing employee). Alvarez, Chen, Farouk remain.

Nice, that's coherent.

Now Q2 recheck: any post-notice ratings? No. Good.

Q2 (a) Dalton: proxy (7+0)/2 = 3.5 → total 10.5 + 3 = 13.5. Yes.

Q5(a): recompute under old rules: performance credit for old rules — the preamble tables show "current performance service credit" years: e.g., 3/3/3 = 12 years; 5/5/5 = 20 years; 5/4/4 = 18; 4/3/3 = 14; 5/4/3 = 16; 4/3/missing = 14. Let me verify a formula: credit = 4 × average? 3/3/3 avg 3 → 12 ✓. 5/5/5 avg 5 → 20 ✓. 5/4/4 avg 4.33 → 17.33 shown 18 (=4×4.33 rounded up). 4/3/3 avg 3.33 → 13.33 shown 14 (round up). 5/4/3 avg 4 → 16 ✓. 4/3 (missing, maybe treated as average of two then?) avg of 4,3 = 3.5 → 14 ✓. So credit = 4 × average, with rounding up to whole years? Actually old rule: additional service credit = number of years based on average summary level: average 5 → 4 years per grade? Hmm 4 × avg means level 5 → 4 years per rating? So each rating contributes 4×(level)/... whatever. Anyway, we can use: credit years = 4 × average rating, rounded up.

For Lee (3,3,3): 12 years → adjusted SCD 1998-03-02 minus 12 = 1986-03-02. Park (5,5,5): 20 years → 2019-07-08 minus 20 = 1999-07-08. Lee earlier → Lee ranked ahead → Park released.

Hmm, but is performance credit added to SCD for all agencies under old rules, or optional? The preamble's example tables apply it. I'll note it's how the preamble illustrates the prior rule and that it was applied within the tenure group/subgroup.

Q5(a)(ii) and (iii): new rules → Lee (9) vs Park (21) → Park higher → Lee released.

Q5(c): events:
1. Which version of the rules applies: the date the agency issues the specific RIF notice (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178: RIF notice issued before/on or after Sept 2, 2026); also 2026-15666 DATES for appeals.
2. End of the four-year period for ratings: the date the agency issues the RIF notices (or, if the agency sets a cutoff date, the cutoff date) — 351.503(c)(1)-(2), (f).
3. Tenure subgroup and retention standing: the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice — 351.502(a)(2)/(3), (b)(2)/(3); 351.507(a)-(b).

Good.

Q9 details:
Step 1: Not compliant. 351.402(b)(1) allows organizational-unit competitive areas approved by agency head/designee (OK), but 351.402(c) requires submission to OPM for approval in advance where the area is established or materially modified within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices. Aug 17 to Oct 13 = 57 days < 90 → must submit description + written statement and obtain OPM approval in advance. Nothing sent to OPM → violation. (Preamble 49179 item 3 says "for OPM review"; text says approval.)

Step 2: In order. 351.202(d)(2)(ii)/(3): career-conditional employee serving initial probationary period is not a competing employee; agency may retain while releasing a competing employee.

Step 3: Not compliant. Supervisory probation is not an "initial probationary period" (351.203 definition excludes the supervisory/managerial probation under part 315 subpart I); 351.502(a)(2) only excludes those serving initial probationary period; preamble 49190-91 confirms career-tenured supervisor on supervisory probation is included and ranked. So Ortiz must be on the register and ranked.

Step 4: Not compliant (partly). 351.503(c)(2)-(4): a cutoff date applies uniformly — after the cutoff no new ratings of record will be put on record and used. Using a post-cutoff rating for one employee because it raised his score violates the uniform and consistent application requirement (351.503(c)(4)). Cutoff: 30 days before Oct 13, 2026 = Sept 13, 2026. The Oct 2 rating is after the cutoff → cannot be used. (If the agency wants to use it, it must not use a cutoff at all and use all ratings through notice date — but 351.503(c)(1) fixes the period at the notice date, and here the agency set a cutoff.) So step 4 is noncompliant; the rating may not be used.

Step 5: Not compliant. 351.503(f)(2) requires proxy = average of the two actual ratings' point values: (7+5)/2 = 6 → 7+5+6 = 18, not a presumed Level 3 (3 points). So her credit is 18, not 15.

Step 6: Not compliant. Additional points for performance awards/QSI are allowed only in the single-pattern/max-level-3 situation (351.503(d)(1)-(3)) and multiple-pattern transmutation (351.503(e)), i.e., only for employees covered by a summary-level system whose highest level is 3; here all employees are rated under one five-level pattern, so no additional points may be added; and in any event the agency may not add points outside the rule. So adding 2 points to QSI recipients is not permitted. (Also must document in advance, etc.)

Step 7: In order. 351.601(c): when tied on performance credit incl. veterans' points, same tenure subgroup, identical service dates, the agency may select any tied employee for release.

Step 8: Not compliant. 351.602(a): agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Reyes holds a temporary promotion ending March 2027 → cannot retain while releasing.

Step 9: In order. 351.702(a)(4)(v): no assessment required if within the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice he occupied the same position (or same grade with substantially the same duties) and received Level 3+ for those duties. Silva held the same position until 2023 and got Level 4 in 2022 → exception applies. (Note: also 351.702(a)(4) other qualification requirements.)

Step 10: Not compliant. 351.702(a)(4)(iii): assessment may not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment. Self-rating questionnaire scored automatically is exactly that. Must use job-analysis-based assessment demonstrating skills (interviews, work exercise, structured resume review, etc.).

Step 11: Not compliant. 351.608(a)(3): exceptions stand alone; may not be sequenced or stacked. So the 60-day undue-interruption exception (351.608(b): not more than 90 days) may be used, but a further 60 days under (g) may not be added; agency may apply the single exception providing the longest period.

Step 12: Not compliant: 351.802(a)(6) (as amended by 2026-15666) requires the notice to state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b) (30 calendar days from the effective date), and the electronic filing system. Telling employees they may appeal to MSPB within 30 days after it takes effect is wrong: appeals go to OPM, filed via OPM's e-filing system, and the 30-day period runs from the effective date of the action (which is roughly consistent timing-wise, but wrong forum and no e-filing info). Cite 351.901(a), 351.802(a)(6), 351.902(a)-(b).

Also note step 1's timing: the RIF notice issued Oct 13 with effect Dec 14 — 62 days notice; 351.801 requires 60 days (not amended; not printed). Hmm — 351.801 notice period requirements aren't printed in these documents, so I shouldn't assert the 60-day rule from memory. I'll avoid.

Now Q1(d): which RIFs the amended rules govern: DATES of 2026-15665 (91 FR 49178): agency that issued a RIF notice before the effective date must process under the regs in effect when the notice was issued; on/after Sept 2, 2026 must apply amended RIF provisions. Also 2026-15666 DATES (appeals) similarly based on specific RIF notice under 351.802 on or after Sept 2, 2026.

Q1(c): corrections to the main final rule: 2026-17335 (Aug 25, 2026; effective Sept 2, 2026; corrects typographical and clerical errors in amendatory instructions and regulatory text) and 2026-18800 (Sept 15, 2026; effective Sept 15, 2026; restores 330.602 "displaced"(1)(i),(ii) inadvertently removed). Note 2026-17338 is a correction to the appeals rule, not the main rule. But should I include it in Q1(c)? The question says "List every correction to that final rule published through today" — "that final rule" = the main retention rule (2026-15665). So only 17335 and 18800. But maybe mention 17338 is a correction to the companion appeals rule (not this one) to avoid confusion.

What does 2026-17335 correct? Let me check its text briefly — I should know specifics ("typographical and clerical errors in amendatory instructions and in the regulatory text"). Let me read it (3 pages, ~120 lines). It could matter for Q11/Q13 (e.g., if it corrected an amendatory instruction). Let me read it.

Budget ~87k. Let's read 2026-17335.

Good enough; I can characterize 2026-17335: corrects amendatory instruction errors (adding instructions 1a-1c for part 316; correcting instruction 5 for 330.202 "Qualified"), Sec. 330.202(5)(iv) list structure, "of this part" references to Sec. 11.2/11.3, a defective list structure in 351.702(a)(4)(iv), citation-form errors, and conforms the part 351 authority citation to the appeals rule version (adding 5 U.S.C. 1103, 1104). It also mentions instruction 36 revises introductory text of 351.802(a) "which has no introductory text" — so the correction presumably adds amendatory instructions; and instruction 39 (353.110(a)(1)) text mismatch.

Note: this confirms a preamble/text mismatch relevant to Q13 maybe: the main rule's preamble (3145-3157) asserts that 351.802(a) previously had an introductory text that was "inadvertently deleted" and that adding the phrase "does not change the substance" — while the correction says 351.802(a) "has no introductory text" in the CFR. Hmm, that's a correction-vs-preamble matter. Could be a Q13 item: preamble says Section 351.802(a) previously read "The notice shall state specifically" and that OPM is restoring an introductory phrase; the correction document states that amendatory instruction 36 "directs revision of introductory text of Sec. 351.802(a), which has no introductory text." That's a preamble (49178/49204-05) vs correction. Q13 is limited to preamble vs amendatory instructions/regulatory text in the same document. So it's fine to use the preamble's assertion that 351.802(a) previously had an introductory text and the amendment merely "makes explicit" — while the actual CFR lacked an introductory text (per 2026-17335, p. 54794). I can present: preamble 49204-05 says the rule is adding back text that "previously read" and that this "does not change the substance," while the correction says the section had no introductory text (so the instruction did not match the CFR) — and the instruction as printed was defective. Slightly technical; I'll include cautiously as an item? It's about the amendatory instruction matching the CFR — the preamble statement "During previous rulemakings, OPM appears to have inadvertently deleted the opening part" is consistent with there being no introductory text. So not a contradiction. Skip.

Now let me spend remaining budget on Q13 with a couple more targeted checks, plus confirm 351.503(d)/(e) preamble vs text? I have enough for Q13 with these items:
1. Erosion of duties: preamble 49190 (1548-1553: 351.201(a)(2) modified; "if the action would take effect after ... announced a RIF ... and the RIF would take effect within 180 days") vs text: 351.201(a)(2) as revised (49218) contains no erosion-of-duties language at all; the operative provision is 351.202(c)(3) (49218), which contains no 180-day element and bars reclassification between announcement and completion where it would adversely affect retention standing. Does another passage state it correctly? Yes — 1576-1580 states the correct standard (no 180 days) and 1547 heading. Good.
2. Competitive area safeguards: preamble 49179 (224-229) "submit a description of the competitive area and provide, for OPM review, a written explanation" vs text 351.402(c) (49220) "to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force"; another passage (49203, 2913-2915) says "OPM approve new or substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less than 90 days" — states approval correctly.
3. Tenure subgroup II: preamble 49196 (2287-2290) "every other competitive service employee who ... is not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less" vs text 351.502(a)(3) (49220) "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316". Also 2262-2278? Actually 1600-1602 states it correctly ("temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D"). Good: another passage correct.
4. Modal rating: preamble 49198 (2466-2474) says 351.503(f) "uses the modal rating concept ... as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)" vs text 351.503(f)(1) (49221) "the modal rating as defined in Sec. 351.203." Different source/cross-reference. Another passage: 2998-3001 refers to "use of the modal rating for employees with no ratings" without a cross-reference. Hmm, is that a "different paragraph" difference? Yes — text points to 351.203, preamble to 351.504(c)(1).
5. Notice requirements: preamble 49198 (2534-2537) "this rule does not change ... the notice requirements in Sec. 351.802, except to conform their provisions to other changes" vs text amending 351.802(a)(2) (adding veterans' preference subgroup) and (a)(3) (link) and (a) intro. Hmm, arguably conforming. Weaker. Also preamble 49205 (3169-3175) explicitly describes those changes. I could omit.
6. 351.202(d) notice: preamble 49190 (1645-1655) says excluded employees' modified notice must include "the action to be taken, the reasons for the action, and its effective date; a link...; information on reemployment rights; and any appeal rights" — text (d)(4) requires content per 351.802(a)(1),(3),(5),(6) and (b) and states that (a)(2) and (a)(4) are not required. Does (a)(3) require "a link"? yes. Consistent-ish. Skip.
7. Another possible: preamble 49198 says "Generally, the three most recent ratings of record received during the 4-year period prior to the date of issuance of reduction in force notices may be considered" — permissive "may" vs text "must be based on" (351.503(c)(1)). Hmm — that's a genuine mismatch in mandatory/permissive tone: text says "must be based on the employee's three most recent summary level ratings," preamble 2312-2313 says "may be considered." Also 2340-2344: "Agencies will list competing employees ... based on each employee's performance credit, which is the sum of the values assigned for their three most recent ratings." Another passage correct. Good item (page 49196 vs 49220-21).
8. 351.504(a) "must be identified" vs preamble? preamble 2475-2485 describes points; no mention of "must". Skip.
9. Maybe: preamble item in Executive Summary (49178, lines 104-109) says excluded employees "can be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted, or reassigned without using RIF procedures" — while 351.202(d)(4) requires a modified RIF notice under 351.801 for such actions. That's a real difference: "without using RIF procedures" vs text requiring written notice under 351.801 with specified content.     "answer": "Places where the preamble of 2026-15665 differs from the amendatory instructions or regulatory text printed in the same document:

1. **Erosion-of-duties reclassification: wrong paragraph and an extra "180 days" trigger.** Preamble (91 FR 49190): "OPM is modifying **Sec. 351.201(a)(2)** to remove from the list of actions that require agencies to use RIF procedures reclassification of an employee's position due to erosion of duties if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF … **and the RIF would take effect within 180 days**." The regulatory text: 351.201(a)(2) as revised (91 FR 49218) contains no erosion-of-duties language at all; the operative provision is **351.202(c)(3)** (91 FR 49218), which bars the reclassification "between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force in the employee's competitive area and the completion of the reduction in force where the reclassification action would adversely affect an employee's retention standing" — **no 180-day element**. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49190 ("this rule will bar agencies from undertaking an erosion-of-duties reclassification between the formal announcement and completion of a RIF if the action would adversely affect an employee's retention standing").

2. **Competitive-area submission: "for OPM review" vs "approval in advance."** Preamble (91 FR 49179, summary of changes from the proposal): "an agency must submit a description of the competitive area and provide, **for OPM review**, a written explanation of the bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area." Regulatory text, 351.402(c) (91 FR 49220): the agency "shall submit a description of the competitive area, along with a written statement explaining the bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area, **to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force**." **Another passage is correct:** 91 FR 49203 ("the requirement in Sec. 351.402(c) that OPM **approve** new or substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less than 90 days prior to the issuance of RIF notices").

3. **Employees excluded "without using RIF procedures" vs a required modified notice.** Executive Summary (91 FR 49178): employees serving initial probationary periods, trial periods, temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less, and Schedule C/G employees "are not 'competing employees' for RIF purposes and can be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted, or reassigned **without using RIF procedures**." Regulatory text, 351.202(d)(4) (91 FR 49218): if such an employee is furloughed for more than 30 days, separated, demoted or reassigned for a 351.201(a)(2) reason (and the action is not merely the expiration of a temporary or time-limited appointment), "the agency **must provide written notice under Sec. 351.801**," including specified content and a statement that the employee is not a competing employee and was not ranked. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49179 (summary item 4) and 91 FR 49190–49191 ("the revised text clarifies that these excluded employees are still subject to the notice provisions of Sec. 351.801").

4. **Tenure subgroup II: "temporary or term appointment" vs "temporary appointment … under subpart D."** Preamble (91 FR 49196): "Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other competitive service employee who, as of the date of the RIF notice, is not serving an initial probationary period or a **temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less**"; the immediately preceding paragraph (91 FR 49196) says the tenure group excludes those serving "an initial probationary period or a **temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR part 316**." Regulatory text, 351.502(a)(3) (91 FR 49220): subgroup II includes employees not in subgroup I who are "not serving an initial probationary period or a **temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316**" — no term appointments, no time-limited appointments, and only subpart D. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49190 ("a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of 5 CFR part 316") and 91 FR 49190–49191 (explaining that the final rule "removes a proposed reference to term appointments under part 316 subpart C").

A later passage (91 FR 49203) refers only to "use of the modal rating," i.e., without either cross-reference, so the preamble nowhere states the point consistently with the text.
