Q1.answer:
**(a) Main final rule.** FR Doc. **2026-15665**, "Reduction in Force," **91 FR 49178–49227**, published **August 3, 2026**, effective **September 2, 2026**, Docket **OPM-2025-0107**, RIN **3206-AO86** (significant).

**(b) Proposed rule it finalized.** FR Doc. **2026-04377**, "Reduction in Force," **91 FR 10904–10934**, published **March 5, 2026** (comments due May 4, 2026), same Docket OPM-2025-0107, same RIN 3206-AO86.

**(c) Corrections to 2026-15665 (two).**
1. **2026-17335**, "Reduction in Force; Correction," **91 FR 54794**, published **August 25, 2026**, effective **September 2, 2026** (same RIN). Corrects typographical/clerical errors in amendatory instructions and regulatory text: adds amendatory instructions 1a–1c fixing three part 316 defects (316.301(c)(1) cross-reference, "30 percent of more," and three 316.403(b) citation/punctuation errors), corrects instruction 5 and the list structure in the "Qualified" definition in 330.202 (and 330.202(5)(iv)), fixes "of this part" references to 5 CFR 11.2/11.3, fixes the list structure in 351.702(a)(4)(iv) and citation-form errors, and conforms the part 351 authority citation to the version in the same-day appeals rule (adding 5 U.S.C. 1103, 1104).
2. **2026-18800**, "Reduction in Force; Correction," **91 FR 58363–58364**, published **September 15, 2026**, effective **September 15, 2026** (Dockets OPM-2025-0107, RIN 3206-AO86). Restores 5 CFR 330.602, definition of "displaced," paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii), which amendatory instruction 11 (91 FR 49217) had inadvertently deleted by setting out only the introductory text of paragraph (1).
(Note: **2026-17338**, 91 FR 54796, Aug. 25, 2026, is also titled "Reduction in Force Appeals; Correction," but it corrects the separate appeals rule, 2026-15666, not 2026-15665.)

**(d) Which RIFs the amended rules govern.** The DATES section of 2026-15665 (91 FR 49178) states: "An agency that issued a RIF notice before the effective date of the rule must process the RIF under the regulations in effect when the RIF notice was issued. An agency that issues a RIF notice on or after the effective date must apply the RIF provisions as amended by this final rule." The dividing line is therefore **issuance of the specific RIF notice** on or after **September 2, 2026**. For appeals, the companion rule uses the same trigger: "applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026" (2026-15666, DATES, 91 FR 49230).

**(e) Other 2026 final rules amending 5 CFR part 351, effective on/after September 2, 2026 (excluding corrections).**
- **2026-15666**, "Reduction in Force Appeals," **91 FR 49230–49267**, published Aug. 3, 2026, effective **Sept. 2, 2026**. Changes part 351: revises **351.802(a)(6)** (notice must state the OPM appeal right, the 351.902(b) time limit, and OPM's e-filing system), revises **351.807(e)**, and replaces **subpart I** wholesale (351.901–351.909: appeals go to OPM, not MSPB). **In force today.**
- **2026-21316**, "Managing Senior Professional Performance," **91 FR 65904**, published Oct. 19, 2026, effective **Nov. 18, 2026**. Changes part 351: revises the **351.203** definition of "Rating of record" and amends **351.503(a)(1)** (adding "the summary performance levels in Sec. 430.505(a)(6)") and **351.503(b)(2)–(3)** (adding part 430 subpart E ratings and equivalency). **Not in force today.**
- **2026-21320**, "Administrative Leave for Workforce Realignment and Other Purposes," **91 FR 65924**, published Oct. 19, 2026, effective **Nov. 18, 2026**. Changes part 351: revises **351.806** (status during the RIF notice period). **Not in force today.**
- Not qualifying: **2026-13715** (91 FR 41521, eff. Aug. 6, 2026) amended part 351 (former 351.504, "430.208(d)" to "430.208(e)") but took effect **before** Sept. 2, 2026 and was superseded by 2026-15665's rewrite of subpart E; **2026-15650** (part 731) and **2026-15654** (parts 11, 230, 315, 432, 751, 752) do not amend part 351; **2026-21319** and **2026-22093** do not amend part 351; corrections 2026-17335, 2026-17338 and 2026-18800 are excluded by the question.
Q1.uncertainty: Whether 2026-21316 and 2026-21320 belong in the list is clear from their CFR-affected fields and amendatory text, but both are **not yet in force** on Nov. 14, 2026, so part 351 as it applies today reflects only 2026-15665 (as corrected) plus 2026-15666. The exact scope of 2026-17335's correction of 351.702(a)(4)(iv) is described only generally as a "defective list structure."

Q2.answer:
**(a) Scores (91 FR 49220–49221 rule; notices Sept. 3, 2026, so the 4-year window is Sept. 3, 2022–Sept. 3, 2026).**
- **Abbott** — career, so competitive service tenure subgroup I (5 CFR 351.502(a)(2)). Ratings 5/4/4: 7+5+5 = **17.0**. No preference: **0** (351.504(a)(3), Subgroup B). **Total 17.0.**
- **Bianchi** — career, subgroup I. Ratings 4/2/3: 5+0+3 = **8.0**. Compensable service-connected disability of 30% or more: **+5** (351.504(a)(1), Subgroup AD). **Total 13.0.**
- **Castillo** — career, subgroup I. Ratings 5/4/4: 7+5+5 = **17.0**. Retired lieutenant colonel, retired pay based on 22 years (20+ years), no disability: not a preference eligible under 351.504(b)(1), (b)(2) or (b)(3), and (b)(4) requires that he be a disabled veteran. **0** (Subgroup B). **Total 17.0.**
- **Dalton** — career, subgroup I. Two ratings, 5 and 2: proxy = (7+0)/2 = **3.5**; credit = 7+0+3.5 = **10.5** (351.503(f)(2)). Preference eligible, no disability: **+3** (351.504(a)(2), Subgroup A). **Total 13.5.**
- **Eze** — term appointment of four years, probation completed, not career or career-conditional: competitive service **tenure subgroup II** (351.502(a)(3); a term appointment of more than one year is not excluded by 351.202(d)). Ratings 4/4/4: 5+5+5 = **15.0**; no preference, 0. **Total 15.0.**
- **Fontaine** — career, subgroup I. One rating, Level 4: 5 x 3 = **15.0** (351.503(f)(3)); no preference, 0. **Total 15.0.**

**(b) Order of retention (one competitive-service register, 351.501(a)–(c)):**
1. **Abbott 17.0** (subgroup I; SCD 5/1/2003)
2. **Castillo 17.0** (subgroup I; SCD 8/1/2012) — tied on 17.0 in the same tenure subgroup, so the earlier SCD ranks ahead (351.501(c)).
3. **Fontaine 15.0** (subgroup I)
4. **Eze 15.0** (subgroup II) — tied on 15.0, so subgroup I is listed ahead of subgroup II (351.501(c)).
5. **Dalton 13.5**
6. **Bianchi 13.0**
**Released (the two lowest): Dalton and Bianchi.**

**(c) Under the earlier rules, Bianchi would have stood ABOVE Abbott.** The preamble describes the prior system (91 FR 49198): employees were "ranked first by tenure group I, II, III; then within each tenure group by veterans' preference subgroup AD, A, B; and only then by years of service as augmented by performance credit." Both are tenure group I, but Bianchi was subgroup AD and Abbott subgroup B, so Bianchi ranked ahead regardless of ratings or SCD. The rule's own before/after examples make the point: "Kai moves from first under current rules to fourth under this final rule because veterans' preference and tenure no longer control ahead of performance" (91 FR 49201).

**(d) What Bianchi may see.** Under 5 CFR 351.506(b)–(c) she may inspect and review any completed records used in the action against her, including **the complete retention register** with the released employee's name and the **names of all other employees listed on that register**, each employee's **performance credit** (351.503) **as augmented by veterans' preference** (351.504), and each employee's **service computation date** (351.505); and the complete registers for **other positions that could affect her competitive level or her assignment rights** (351.506(c)(2)). Her representative may inspect on her behalf (351.506(b)(1)). She was also entitled to the notice content in 351.802(a)(2) (competitive area, competitive level, veterans' preference subgroup, tenure group and subgroup, service date, three most recent ratings of record). Records must be kept at least two years (351.506(f)).
Q2.uncertainty: The rule expressly allows a two-rating proxy to end in .5 (351.503(f)(2)), so Dalton's 13.5 is textual, not an estimate; nothing in the documents requires rounding. No cutoff date was in use. Eze's subgroup would change only if his term appointment were one year or less, which the scenario excludes.

Q3.answer:
**(a) Status, points, subgroup (5 CFR 351.504 as revised by 2026-15665, 91 FR 49222):**
- **A (LTC, 22 yrs, retired pay based on length of service, no disability): NOT a preference eligible.** He meets none of 351.504(b)(1)–(3), and because he retired at the rank of major or above, 351.504(b)(4) supplies eligibility only if he is a *disabled* veteran who also meets (b)(1)–(3). Points **0**; **Subgroup B** (351.504(a)(3)).
- **B (Navy commander, 21 yrs, length-of-service retired pay, 40 percent compensable): NOT a preference eligible.** Commander is the equivalent of major or above; under 351.504(b)(4) he must be a disabled veteran **and** meet one of (b)(1)–(3). He is a disabled veteran, but (b)(1) fails (retirement is not based on disability), (b)(2) fails (retired pay is based on 20 or more years of active service), and (b)(3) fails (not continuously employed since Nov. 30, 1964). Points **0**; **Subgroup B**.
- **C (major, disability retirement for an injury in the line of duty as a direct result of armed conflict, 60 percent): preference eligible.** 351.504(b)(1)(i) is met and 351.504(b)(4) is satisfied. Compensable disability of 30 percent or more: **+5 points** (351.504(a)(1)); **Subgroup AD**.
- **D (master sergeant, 24 yrs, length-of-service retired pay, no disability): NOT a preference eligible.** (b)(1) fails; (b)(2) fails because his retired pay is based on 20 or more years of full-time active service; (b)(3) fails. (b)(4) and (b)(5) do not create eligibility for someone below major. Points **0**; **Subgroup B**.
- **E (staff sergeant, medical retirement after 16 yrs for a training injury not from armed conflict or an instrumentality of war, 10 percent): preference eligible.** (b)(1) fails, but (b)(2) is met because his retired pay is based on disability and is **not** based on 20 or more years of full-time active service. Disability is under 30 percent: **+3 points** (351.504(a)(2)); **Subgroup A**.

**(b) Service computation dates (5 CFR 351.505(b)–(d)).**
- **Employee A:** he is a retired member of a uniformed service covered by 351.504(b) and is not a preference eligible, so 351.505(b)(2)(i) limits credit to active service during a war or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge was authorized: **2 years**. SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 minus 2 years = **September 7, 2008** (351.505(d)(2)). The other 20 years are not creditable.
- **Employee C:** he is a preference eligible under 351.504(b) (351.505(b)(2)(ii)), so all 14 years are creditable. SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 minus 14 years = **September 7, 1996**.

**(c) Role of the AD/A/B subgroups.** Under the amended rules the subgroups have **no ordering effect**: employees are ranked within each tenure group by performance credit augmented by veterans' preference points (351.501(b)); ties are broken by tenure subgroup (I before II) and then by earliest SCD (351.501(c)). The subgroups are identification labels that must appear on the register (351.504(a)) and in the notice (351.802(a)(2)). Veterans' preference now operates only as +5, +3 or 0 points.
Q3.basis: 5 CFR 351.504(a)–(b), 351.501(b)–(c), 351.505(a)–(d), 351.802(a)(2), as revised by 2026-15665 (91 FR 49220–49223, 49226); preamble at 91 FR 49196–49197 (ranking and points), 49202–49203 (length of service); the proposed rule's erroneous cross-reference "Sec. 351.503(b)" was corrected to "Sec. 351.504(b)" in the final text (compare 2026-04377, 91 FR 10930, with 2026-15665, 91 FR 49222).
Q3.uncertainty: 351.505(b)(2) is worded "a retired member of a uniformed service who is covered by Sec. 351.504(b)." Read literally, a non-preference-eligible retiree might be said not to be "covered by" 351.504(b) and would then get full active-duty credit under (b)(1), making A's SCD Sept. 7, 1988. The better reading, and the only one that gives (b)(2)(ii) independent meaning and tracks 5 U.S.C. 3502(a)(B), is that (b)(2) governs all retired members and full credit is given only to those who are preference eligible; on that reading A's SCD is Sept. 7, 2008. 5 U.S.C. 3502 itself is not printed in these documents, so the statute cannot be checked here.

Q4.answer:
**(a) Farah, no cutoff: performance credit = 13.** Notices Sept. 3, 2026, so the four-year period is **Sept. 3, 2022–Sept. 3, 2026** (351.503(c)(1)); all five ratings fall inside it. The three most recent are Aug. 10, 2026 (Level 5) = 7, Nov. 14, 2025 (Level 3) = 3, Nov. 15, 2024 (Level 3) = 3. 7+3+3 = **13** (351.503(a)). The 2022 and 2023 Level 4 ratings are older and are not used.

**(b) With a cutoff 45 days before Sept. 3, 2026: cutoff = July 20, 2026; credit = 11.** Counting: Sept. 3 minus 3 = Aug. 31 (3 days); minus 31 = July 31 (34); minus 11 = **July 20, 2026**. Under 351.503(c)(2) credit is based on the three most recent ratings received during the four years before the **cutoff** (July 20, 2022–July 20, 2026), and no rating after the cutoff is used. In-window ratings: Nov. 18, 2022 (L4), Nov. 20, 2023 (L4), Nov. 15, 2024 (L3), Nov. 14, 2025 (L3). The Aug. 10, 2026 Level 5 is after the cutoff and is disregarded. Three most recent: L3 (2025) = 3, L3 (2024) = 3, L4 (2023) = 5, total **11**.

**(c) The July 15, 2026 rating cannot be used.** 351.503(c)(3) requires both that the rating have been "issued to the employee, with all appropriate reviews and signatures" **and** that it be "on record (i.e., the rating of record is available for use by the office responsible for establishing retention registers)." The signature requirement was met on July 15 (before the July 20 cutoff), but the rating was not on record until Aug. 15, after the cutoff, and 351.503(c)(2) says that after the cutoff "no new ratings of record will be put on record and used for purposes of this subpart." It is therefore unusable.

**(d) Gina, no cutoff: performance credit = 12.** Four-year period Sept. 3, 2022–Sept. 3, 2026; the Aug. 15, 2022 Level 5 is **outside** it. Two ratings remain: Nov. 15, 2024 (L4) = 5 and Nov. 14, 2025 (L3) = 3. Proxy = (5+3)/2 = **4** (351.503(f)(2)); credit = 5+3+4 = **12**.

**(e) Hank: credit is based on the modal rating.** 351.503(f)(1): the credit of an employee with no rating of record during the four-year period "must be based on the modal rating as defined in Sec. 351.203 for the summary level pattern that applies to the employee's official position of record at the time of the reduction in force." The preamble describes this as carrying forward "the modal rating concept ..., as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)" (91 FR 49198), i.e., the summary level most commonly assigned under the applicable pattern. His lack of ratings is not a bar to competition; he is scored at the modal value, using the point values in 351.503(a)(1). The most defensible reading is that the modal level is used for the missing three years (3 x the modal level's points), consistent with 351.503(f)(3).
Q4.uncertainty: **No definition of "modal rating" is printed.** Amendatory instruction 19 adds "Agency," "Competitive service tenure group," "Excepted service tenure group," "Government obligation," "Initial probationary period," "Military spouse," "Reduction in force," "Restoration protected employee" and "Trial period" to 351.203, but not "modal rating," and the CFR is unavailable, so the cross-reference cannot be verified. The rule also does not say whether the modal value is applied once or three times; the analogy to 351.503(f)(3) supports three times, but the text is silent.

Q5.answer:
**(a)(i) Notices August 28, 2026: the earlier rules apply, and PARK is released.** 2026-15665 DATES: a RIF notice issued before Sept. 2, 2026 is processed "under the regulations in effect when the RIF notice was issued." Under the prior rules as described at 91 FR 49198–49201, both are tenure group I and both are veterans' preference subgroup B, so they are ranked within the subgroup by service computation date as augmented by performance credit ("adjusted SCD"). Using the conversion in the preamble's "Current Rules" tables (credit = 4 years x average rating; 3/3/3 = 12 years, 5/5/5 = 20 years): Lee 1998-03-02 minus 12 years = **1986-03-02**; Park 2019-07-08 minus 20 years = **1999-07-08**. Lee's adjusted SCD is earlier, so Lee ranks ahead and **Park is released**.

**(ii) Notices September 2, 2026: the amended rules apply, and LEE is released.** The rule is effective Sept. 2, 2026 and governs a notice issued on or after the effective date. Lee: 3+3+3 = **9**, no points. Park: 7+7+7 = **21**, no points (351.503(a); 351.504(a)(3)). Park ranks first; **Lee is released**.

**(iii) Notices September 3, 2026: same as (ii), LEE is released** (9 vs 21).

**(b) No, retention standing is not recalculated.** 5 CFR 351.507(a) fixes the standing of each released employee "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice" (Sept. 3, 2026). 5 CFR 351.805(b) provides that an amended notice issued solely to state a later effective date "is not a new specific reduction in force notice for purposes of Sec. 351.507 and does not require the agency to redetermine or recalculate retention standing under subpart E." Lee's Oct. 15, 2026 Level 5 rating postdates the notice he received and cannot be used; the release of Lee stands, subject only to the duty to correct an error under 351.507(c), which is not implicated here.

**(c) The three triggering events.**
1. **Which version of the rules applies — the date the agency issues the specific RIF notice** (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178: notice before vs on or after Sept. 2, 2026; for appeals, 2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230).
2. **The end of the four-year period for ratings — the date the agency issues the RIF notices, or the agency-established cutoff date if one is used** (351.503(c)(1)–(2), (c)(4)(i), and (f), 91 FR 49220–49221).
3. **Tenure subgroup and retention standing — the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice** (351.502(a)(2), (a)(3), (b)(2), (b)(3); 351.507(a)–(b), 91 FR 49220, 49223).
Q5.basis: 2026-15665 DATES (91 FR 49178); 5 CFR 351.501–351.503, 351.507, 351.805(b) as revised (91 FR 49220–49223, 49226); preamble descriptions of the prior rules and the before/after examples at 91 FR 49198–49202; 2026-16456, 91 FR 51997 (same notice-based trigger for RIF appeals).
Q5.uncertainty: For the earlier rules the documents do not print the former regulatory text; they describe the prior system narratively and through example tables, and the preamble notes that some proposed-rule tables "contained errors" (91 FR 49199). The result in (i) is robust: Lee's unadjusted SCD is 21 years earlier than Park's, and the described conversion cannot produce more than about 24 years of credit, so Park cannot overtake Lee on service.

Q6.answer:
**(a) Jordan (GS-13, one-grade interval; Level 2; no preference; career, so competitive service tenure subgroup I).** A released employee with a current annual rating of Level 2 (Minimally Satisfactory) or higher has assignment rights (351.701(a)). Rights reach positions (i) held by an employee with **lower retention standing in the same tenure group** (351.701(b)(1)); (ii) **not more than three grades below** his position, measured by the released employee's own grade progression, which for a one-grade interval GS position means GS-12, GS-11 and GS-10 (351.701(b)(2), (d)(1)–(2)); (iii) in the **same competitive area** and with the **same type of work schedule** (351.701(a)); and (iv) for which he is qualified (351.701(b)(3)).
- **Available:** #1 (GS-12, Ellis, lower standing), #2 (GS-11, Frank, lower), #3 (GS-10, Gale, lower).
- **Not available:** #4 GS-9 (four grades below, outside the three-grade limit); #5 (Ito has higher standing, 351.701(b)(1)); #6 (part-time, a different work schedule, 351.701(a)); #7 (different competitive area, 351.701(a)).
- **What must be offered:** the position requiring "no reduction, or the least possible reduction, in representative rate," which is **#1, the GS-12 held by Ellis**.

**(b) If Jordan has a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more:** the limit becomes **five grades** (351.701(b)(2)), so **#4 (GS-9, Hana)** also becomes available. The required offer does not change: the agency must still offer the **GS-12 (#1)**, the least possible reduction.

**(c) If his current annual rating of record is Level 1:** 351.701(a) applies only to an employee with a current annual rating of "minimally satisfactory (Level 2) or equivalent, or higher." A Level 1 employee has **no assignment rights** to any of the seven positions; the agency furloughs or separates him under subpart F.

**(d) If Jordan and all seven holders are in the excepted service:** 351.701(a) covers "a competitive service tenure group employee," so **no assignment rights arise** under part 351. Under **351.705(a)** an agency may, at its discretion, adopt provisions giving excepted-service competing employees assignment rights to positions under the same appointing authority "on the same basis as" 351.701; absent such a provision, none of the positions is available and Jordan is released.

**(e) The old handbook's two ideas.** The 2026 preamble (91 FR 49203) says the rule consolidates former 351.701(b) and (c) and eliminates "the separate concepts of an employee 'bumping' another employee in a lower subgroup, and 'retreating' to the position of a lower-ranked employee in the same subgroup." Both are replaced by a single right: assignment to a position held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, not more than three (or five) grades below, for which the employee is qualified (351.701(b)). The preamble also states that OPM is eliminating former **351.701(d)**: the old restriction on employees with a Level 2 rating "from obtaining assignment to positions held by employees with a higher performance rating ... is no longer necessary." So the handbook's rule that a Level 2 employee cannot take a position held by someone with a higher rating is no longer the rule; what controls is the comparison of retention standing, in which ratings appear only as performance credit.
Q6.uncertainty: 351.703, referenced in 351.701(b)(3), was not amended by 2026-15665 and is therefore not printed in the Federal Register, so its content cannot be verified. The documents also do not address how an agency chooses among several released employees who each have a right to the same position.

Q7.answer:
**(a) The Merit Systems Protection Board hears it.** 2026-15666 applies "only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026" (DATES, 91 FR 49230). Morgan's notice issued **August 31, 2026**, so her appeal remains at MSPB. Documents that bear on the answer: **2026-15666** (DATES at 91 FR 49230; preamble at 91 FR 49248 stating that an appeal of an action for which the notice issued before that date, "including an appeal pending before the MSPB, continues to be adjudicated by the MSPB," and at 91 FR 49262); **2026-17338**, its correction (91 FR 54796, effective Sept. 2, 2026), which corrects text but not the applicability date; and **MSPB's 2026-16456** ("Appellate Jurisdiction Update II," 91 FR 51997, effective Sept. 2, 2026), which removed MSPB's RIF appeal paragraph from 5 CFR 1201.3(a) but states that MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals not covered by OPM's rule.

**(b) OPM hears it; she must file through OPM's electronic filing system; the last day is Tuesday, January 19, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET.** Under 351.901(a) an employee "separated ... by a reduction-in-force action taken under this part may appeal that action to OPM." Filing is exclusively through "the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website"; e-mail or postal filings are not accepted absent good cause and OPM approval (351.902(a), (c)). The deadline is within 30 calendar days from the effective date of the action, timely if e-filed by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the 30th calendar day (351.902(b)); the first day counted is the day after the effective date, and if the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday the period extends to the first workday (351.902(b)(1)). Counting: effective date **Friday, Dec. 18, 2026**, so day 1 = Dec. 19; Dec. 19–31 = days 1–13; Jan. 1, 2027 = day 14; **Jan. 17, 2027 = day 30**, a Sunday, so the next workday is **Monday, Jan. 18, 2027**, which is Martin Luther King, Jr. Day and a Federal holiday. The period therefore runs to **Tuesday, January 19, 2027**, 11:59 p.m. ET.

**(c) What she must prove; hearing.** By a preponderance of the evidence she must prove (1) the timeliness of the written appeal; (2) OPM jurisdiction; (3) that the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIF actions under part 351; and (4) that the failure **prejudiced** her by causing the appealed action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)). She is **not entitled to a hearing**: review "must be based solely on the developed written record unless OPM determines that a hearing is necessary and efficient," defined as an insufficiently developed record or a material disputed issue of witness credibility (351.905(c)).

**(d) The union cannot use the negotiated grievance procedure.** 351.901(c)(1)–(2): the subpart I procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action, and a RIF action taken under part 351 "and any matter relating to an appeal of such an action, may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration." The preamble (91 FR 49245) adds that the rule does **not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs** or adjudicate particular CBA disputes: "when agreements are renegotiated, this governmentwide rule will limit agencies' duty and ability to bargain for provisions that create a direct RIF appeal process inconsistent with part 351," and questions about particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability, or unfair labor practices "remain matters for resolution under chapter 71 by the appropriate forum."

**(e) No.** 351.901(c)(4): "A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart." (Preamble, 91 FR 49243, explains that judicial review would be unavailable even if the rule were silent.)

**(f) Yes, she may still appeal, by April 9, 2027.** 351.902(b)(3) applies where, before the filing period expires, the employee timely filed a complaint, appeal or other matter within the independent jurisdiction of an entity listed in 351.901(c) (OSC is listed), and the final decision on that matter "materially affects the employee's retention standing, order of release, assignment rights, or other rights under this part." She may then appeal "within 30 calendar days after the date on which the decision on that matter becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review." Her OSC complaint was filed before her Jan. 19, 2027 deadline and ended in a final decision on **March 10, 2027** correcting the rating; assuming that is the date the decision became final and unreviewable, the appeal is due **April 9, 2027** (March 10 plus 30 calendar days). OPM decides in its sole and exclusive discretion whether the decision materially affects her rights under part 351.

**(g) The provision that decides between (a) and (b)** is the **DATES** paragraph of 2026-15666 at **91 FR 49230**: "Effective September 2, 2026. This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026." It is restated in that document's preamble at **91 FR 49248** and **91 FR 49262**, and mirrored on the Board's side in 2026-16456 at **91 FR 51997–51998**.
Q7.uncertainty: The 30-day computation assumes the action's effective date is Dec. 18, 2026 and that the weekend/holiday rule in 351.902(b)(1) extends the deadline to Tuesday, Jan. 19, 2027 (Jan. 18, 2027 being the Martin Luther King, Jr. Day holiday; the regulation does not itself list holidays). For (f), whether the March 10, 2027 OSC decision is "final and no longer subject to further administrative review" on that date is for OPM to determine; if finality occurred later, the deadline shifts.

Q8.answer:
**(a) Two versions.**
- **In force today (Nov. 14, 2026):** the pre-amendment 5 CFR 351.806, under which agencies are directed to keep a RIF-affected employee **in duty status during the notice period "when possible,"** and which contains the longstanding emergency provision allowing annual leave with or without consent, leave without pay with consent, or a nonpay status without consent when in an emergency the agency lacks work or funds for all or part of the notice period. The 2026 documents quote the "when possible" language and describe the emergency provision as "longstanding" and unchanged (2026-13073, 91 FR 39034; 2026-21320, 91 FR 65933, 65936). That version contains **no express administrative-leave paragraph**; administrative leave was governed instead by 5 U.S.C. 6329a and part 630, subpart N.
- **Adopted but not yet in force:** FR Doc. **2026-21320**, "Administrative Leave for Workforce Realignment and Other Purposes," **91 FR 65924** (proposed rule 2026-13073, 91 FR 39032, June 29, 2026), **effective November 18, 2026**. It revises 351.806 to read: (a) *General*: "Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period"; (b) *Administrative leave*: "Nothing in this section precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines that such leave is appropriate and the use of administrative leave is consistent with part 630, subpart N of this chapter"; (c) *Emergency lack of work or funds*: the longstanding annual leave/LWOP/nonpay provision, restated (91 FR 65939).

**(b) Consent and duration under the adopted text and its companion leave provision.** **No employee consent is required.** Neither 351.806(b) nor new **630.1403(c)(10)** mentions consent; the agency may provide leave "at its sole and exclusive discretion" (630.1403(c)) when it "determines it is in the Government's best interests" (630.1403(c)(10)), and "sole and exclusive discretion" is defined as discretion that "may not be limited or conditioned by any agreement" (630.1402). **Yes, there is a limit:** the leave is confined to the RIF notice period — 630.1403(c)(10) permits it "during the period between receipt of the RIF notice and the RIF separation," and 351.806(b) permits it "for all or part of the notice period." Subpart N's general limits also apply, including the norm of "brief or short periods ... usually for not more than 1 workday" with longer periods permitted in the 630.1403(c) circumstances, and the review and approval requirement in 630.1403(a)(5)(ii) where the type and amount of leave are not already authorized by written agency policy (91 FR 65940).

**(c) What OPM says allowed administrative leave before the adopted text takes effect.** OPM's position is that administrative leave during a RIF notice period was **already permissible** and that the amendment merely clarifies it. The proposed rule says the revision "clarif[ies] that use of administrative leave during a RIF notice period is permissible, if an agency determines that there is justification for putting the RIF-affected employee in nonduty status," and that it "is consistent with OPM's Agency Policy Template, which specifically stated that an agency may provide administrative leave during a RIF notice period, if it determines such use supports agency interests" (2026-13073, 91 FR 39034). The final rule says the new (b) "confirms—consistent with the Agency Policy Template" that authority and that "[n]othing in the revision permits use of administrative leave inconsistent with subpart N of part 630" (2026-21320, 91 FR 65933; footnote citing CPM 2025-12 at 91 FR 65926).

**(d) No effect on retention standing, notice, or appeal rights.** Retention standing is determined by the subpart E factors as of the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice (351.507(a)); duty status is not a listed factor (351.501). The notice rules (351.801–351.802) and appeal rights (subpart I) are unaffected. OPM says so expressly: the new 630.1403(c)(10) and revised 351.806 "address only whether an employee may be placed in a paid, non-duty status during a RIF notice period. Those provisions do not alter the substantive or procedural requirements governing RIF, which continue to apply in full whenever an agency conducts a RIF. Nothing in this rule authorizes an agency to bypass RIF competition, retention registers, or appeal rights" (91 FR 65926).
Q8.uncertainty: The **full current text** of 5 CFR 351.806 is not printed in any 2026 Federal Register document (it is only described and republished in revised form), so today's paragraph lettering cannot be verified line by line; only the "when possible" standard and the emergency provision are documented. Subpart N was largely promulgated earlier and is not reproduced, so any outer numeric limit on this use cannot be confirmed beyond the notice-period boundary and the "usually not more than 1 workday" norm.

Q9.answer:
**Not in order: steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12. In order: steps 2, 7, 9.** (Notices Oct. 13, 2026; effect Dec. 14, 2026, so the amended rules apply; a 30-day cutoff is **Sept. 13, 2026**.)

**1 — Does not comply.** 351.402(b)(1) allows an organizational unit on the agency's official chart, approved by the agency head or designee (with no delegation below headquarters level), which is satisfied. But **351.402(c)** requires that, when an agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices, it "shall submit a description of the competitive area, along with a written statement explaining the bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area, **to OPM for approval in advance** of the reduction in force." Aug. 17 to Oct. 13 is 57 days. **Required:** submit the description and justification to OPM and obtain approval before the RIF. (The preamble at 91 FR 49179 describes this as submission "for OPM review"; the text requires approval and controls.)

**2 — In order.** A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is **not a competing employee** (351.202(d)(2)(ii)), and the agency "may retain such an employee while releasing a competing employee" (351.202(d)(3)).

**3 — Does not comply.** A supervisory or managerial probation is **not** an "initial probationary period": 351.203 defines initial probationary period as the period described in 5 CFR 11.2 and expressly "does not include the probationary period applicable on initial appointment to a supervisory or managerial position described in subpart I of part 315." 351.502(a)(2) excludes only those serving an initial probationary period. The preamble (91 FR 49190–49191) states that a career-tenured employee on supervisory probation "would be included in the RIF in the supervisory or managerial position." **Required:** Ortiz must be placed on the competitive-service register and ranked.

**4 — Does not comply.** 351.503(c)(2) permits a cutoff date "after which no new ratings of record will be put on record and used," and 351.503(c)(4) requires uniform and consistent application within the competitive area. With a Sept. 13, 2026 cutoff, Mr. Pruitt's Oct. 2, 2026 rating could not be put on record and used for RIF purposes; using it only because it raised his score, while using no other post-cutoff rating, is inconsistent. **Required:** apply the cutoff consistently (excluding the Oct. 2 rating) or forgo a cutoff altogether and use all ratings received through the notice date.

**5 — Does not comply.** For two actual ratings 351.503(f)(2) requires a proxy equal to the average of the two point values: (7 + 5)/2 = 6, giving 7 + 5 + 6 = **18**. The agency substituted a presumed Level 3 (3 points), producing 15. **Required:** credit of 18.

**6 — Does not comply.** Additional points for performance awards or a QSI are authorized only under 351.503(d)(1)–(3) (single pattern whose highest summary level is Level 3) and 351.503(e)(1)–(2) (transmutation between patterns). All these employees are rated under one five-level pattern, so no additional points may be added; a written policy cannot supply authority the rule withholds. **Required:** score strictly under 351.503(a).

**7 — In order.** 351.601(c): where employees in the same tenure group have identical performance credits as augmented by veterans' preference, are in the same tenure subgroup, and have identical service dates, "the agency may select any tied employee for release."

**8 — Does not comply.** 351.602(a): an agency "may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with ... [a] specifically limited temporary or term promotion." **Required:** Mr. Reyes may not block the release; the temporary promotion must be ended or the competition run without retaining him in the level.

**9 — In order.** 351.702(a)(4)(v) excuses an assessment where, during the five-year period ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, the employee occupied the same position (or one at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualification requirements and conditions of employment) and received a rating of Level 3 or higher for those duties. Silva held the same position until 2023 and received a Level 4 in 2022, within five years of Oct. 13, 2026.

**10 — Does not comply.** 351.702(a)(4)(iii) requires an assessment that "does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment," and (a)(4)(i)–(ii) require a job-analysis-based assessment allowing demonstration of job-related skills (structured interview, work-related exercise, structured resume review, etc.). **Required:** a qualifying assessment in place of the automatically scored self-rating questionnaire, unless 351.702(a)(4)(v) applies to a given employee.

**11 — Does not comply.** 351.608(a)(3): "Each exception under a paragraph in this section stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked in combination with another exception. If an agency determines that it can approve more than one exception for an employee, the agency may apply the exception that provides for the longest period of retention." The undue-interruption exception is capped at 90 days (351.608(b)) and the "other" exception at 90 days (351.608(g)). **Required:** one exception only, of the longest available period (at most 90 days), not 60 plus 60.

**12 — Does not comply.** For a notice issued after Sept. 2, 2026, appeals go to **OPM**, not MSPB (351.901(a); 2026-15666). 351.802(a)(6) as revised by 2026-15666 (91 FR 49263) requires the notice to state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b), and the electronic filing system on OPM's website through which an appeal must be filed. The timing statement is roughly right (30 days from the effective date, 351.902(b)), but the forum and filing method are wrong. **Required:** corrected notice language.
Q9.uncertainty: The documents prescribe no remedy for the competitive-area defect beyond obtaining OPM approval in advance, and do not say whether late approval could cure it. Whether the wrong-forum notice statement in step 12 prejudiced any employee is a question under 351.901(b)(4) that the text does not resolve.

Q10.answer:
**(a) On September 10, 2026 the definition of "displaced" in 330.602, paragraph (1), contained only its introductory text:** "A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:" — **with no subparagraphs.** Paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii), which describe when a competitive-service employee is displaced, had been **inadvertently deleted** by amendatory instruction 11 of the August 3, 2026 final rule (91 FR 49217), which "directed that paragraph (1) ... be revised, and set out only the introductory text of that paragraph as the revised text," although "OPM intended to revise only the introductory text ... and to leave paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) ... unchanged" (2026-18800, 91 FR 58363).

**(b) The change.** FR Doc. **2026-18800**, "Reduction in Force; Correction," **91 FR 58363–58364**, published and effective **September 15, 2026**, restored (1)(i) and (1)(ii) "as they read before the final rule." OPM found **good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)** to act without prior notice and comment because the document "makes no substantive change to the regulations": it "restores regulatory text that was in effect before September 2, 2026, that OPM did not propose to remove, and that the final rule did not discuss removing; notice and comment are therefore unnecessary," and it found good cause under **5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)** to make the correction effective upon publication. OPM characterized the action as a **correction**: it called instruction 11 an inadvertent removal, said "[w]ithout these paragraphs, the definition is incomplete," and stated that the document "restores those paragraphs" — i.e., it treated the change as restoring pre-existing text, not as new policy.

**(c) After September 15, 2026.** Paragraph (1)(i) now covers a current competitive-service employee in the competitive service tenure group at GS-15 or below "who: (i) Received a reduction in force (RIF) separation notice under part 351 ... and has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G ... of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated."
- **Full-time offer with a lower representative rate, declined:** she is **still "displaced."** A declination removes CTAP eligibility only if the declined position had the same type of work schedule **and** a representative rate at least as high as her present position; a lower rate does not meet that test.
- **Same representative rate (full-time), declined:** the offer does meet the test, so she would **not** be "displaced" under (1)(i), and her CTAP eligibility on that basis ends.
Q10.basis: 5 CFR 330.602, definition of "displaced" (1)(i)–(ii), as revised by 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363–58364); 2026-15665 amendatory instruction 11 (91 FR 49217); 2026-18800 preamble (Background, Need for Correction, Administrative Procedure Act), 91 FR 58363.
Q10.uncertainty: Whether a position with the same representative rate but a different full-time tour counts turns on the meaning of "same type of work schedule" (full-time, part-time, intermittent, seasonal), which the printed text does not define. The restored (1)(ii) is only summarized in the correction's preamble, not printed in full in these documents.

Q11.answer:
Real differences between the proposed regulatory text (2026-04377, 91 FR 10926–10934) and the final regulatory text (2026-15665, 91 FR 49218–49227):

1. **351.202(d)(1)(ii).** Proposed: exclusion for "[a]n employee serving a trial period **as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice**." Final: "An employee serving a trial period" — the temporal anchor was dropped.
2. **351.202(d)(1)(iii)–(iv).** Proposed: "(iii) Schedule C appointments; and (iv) Schedule G appointments." Final: "(iii) An employee serving under a Schedule C appointment; and (iv) An employee serving under a Schedule G appointment" — describing employees rather than appointments.
3. **351.202(d)(2)(iii).** Proposed: "An employee serving on a **temporary or term** appointment of 1 year or less under **subpart C or D** of part 316." Final: "An employee serving under a **temporary** appointment of one (1) year or less under **subpart D** of part 316." Term appointments of a year or less are no longer excluded and subpart C is dropped.
4. **351.202(d)(3) and new (d)(4).** Proposed (3): excluded employees "may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned **without regard to the provisions of this part**." Final (3): they may be so treated "without determining the employee's retention standing under subparts D and E ..., applying the order-of-release provisions in subpart F ..., or providing assignment rights under subpart G ..., **provided the action is otherwise consistent with the terms of the employee's appointment and applicable law**"; the final rule also adds **paragraph (4)** requiring a written notice under 351.801 with specified content.
5. **351.203, "Furlough."** Proposed included the trailing clause "and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action"; the final definition ends at "...not known by the agency at the outset of the furlough."
6. **351.203 — definition added in the final text.** The final rule adds "**Restoration protected employee** means a competing employee restored or reemployed following uniformed service who, as of the date of a specific reduction in force notice, remains entitled under Sec. 353.209(b) ... to retention for six (6) months or one (1) year after restoration." The proposed rule's instruction 19 did not add this definition.
7. **351.204.** Proposed: agencies are responsible for "following and applying" the regulations. Final adds "and for ensuring that such regulations are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles set forth in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b)."
8. **351.402 — new paragraph (c).** The proposed rule amended only paragraph (b); the final rule also adds (c) (submission to OPM and advance approval for a competitive area established or materially modified within 90 days before specific notices).
9. **351.502(a)(2), (a)(3), (b)(2), (b)(3) — "issues" vs "receives."** Proposed used "as of the date the agency **issues** a specific reduction in force notice" in all four places; the final text uses "as of the date the employee **receives** a specific reduction in force notice."
10. **351.503(a)(1) — label.** Proposed: "0 for a Level 2 (**Minimally Successful** or equivalent)." Final: "Minimally **Satisfactory**."
11. **351.503(d) and (e)(2) — appraisal-system references.** The final text adds, in describing the pattern D/pass-fail system, "authorized under 430.208(d) **prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521**" (in both (d) and (e)(2)), tying the reference to the pre-July 7, 2026 patterns.
12. **351.505(b)(2) — cross-reference to a different section.** Proposed: "a retired member of a uniformed service who is covered by **Sec. 351.503(b)**." Final: "... covered by **Sec. 351.504(b)**." (351.503 is Performance; 351.504 is Veterans' preference.)
13. **351.506(d).** Proposed: an employee without a specific RIF notice "has no right to review the agency's retention registers and related records." Final adds "**under this section**" and a second sentence: "This paragraph does not limit any right of access available under another statute or regulation."
14. **351.605.** Proposed put the notice requirements and the assignment-rights bar inside paragraph (b). Final restructures: (b) retains the release/no-ranking rule and the reference to 351.608(c)–(f); a **new (c)** contains the notice rule (written notice "in accordance with Sec. 351.801," identifying the competitive area being abolished, with the no-ranking statement); and a **new (d)** separately states that no retention register is required and that assignment rights "must not" be applied.
15. **351.606(a).** Proposed: a single sentence — "When an agency applies Sec. 351.601, it shall give retention priorities over other competing employees to each competing employee entitled under **Sec. 351.209(b)** to retention for ... 6 months or 1 year after restoration." Final replaces it with paragraphs (a)(1)–(6): it applies when an agency applies "Sec. 351.601 **or Sec. 351.605**," cites **Sec. 353.209(b)**, requires the agency first to determine ordinary standing and then apply the exception, bars release "if another competing employee may be released instead," requires reassignment rather than separation where no other employee may be released, provides for OPM placement assistance, states what the paragraph does not do, and adds a documentation requirement.
16. **351.608(a)(2) — cross-reference to a different subpart.** Proposed: "a Career Transition Assistance Plan established under part 330, **subpart E**." Final: "part 330, **subpart F**."
17. **351.701(a).** Proposed: "minimally **successful** (Level 2) or equivalent, or higher." Final: "minimally **satisfactory** (Level 2) or equivalent, or higher," plus a "(a) General." caption and the words "in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section."
18. **351.702(a)(4)(iii).** Proposed: "Does not **solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination**." Final: "Does not **consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment**."
19. **351.702(a)(4)(iv).** Proposed used subparagraphs "(A) It demonstrates ...; and (B) Is relevant ..."; the final text uses inline "(1) it demonstrates job-related technical skills, abilities and knowledge, and (2) is relevant ...".
20. **351.702(a)(4)(v) — new in the final text.** The final rule adds an exception from the assessment requirement where, during the five-year period ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, the employee occupied the same or substantially the same position and received a Level 3 or higher rating for those duties. The proposed rule had no such paragraph.
21. **351.802(a) introductory text.** The final rule adds "Except as otherwise provided in this part, a specific written notice under Sec. 351.801 must include:" (instruction 36). The proposed rule did not amend the introductory text.
22. **351.802(a)(2).** Proposed: "... competitive level, **veteran status**, tenure group and subgroup...". Final: "... competitive level, **veterans' preference subgroup**, tenure group and subgroup...".
23. **351.802(a)(3).** Proposed: "A link to part 351 of this chapter **and access** to the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force being taken." Final: "A link to 5 CFR part 351 **and information on how to access** the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force being taken."
24. **351.504(a)(1)–(3) — mandatory rather than hortatory.** Proposed: the 30%-disabled "should be identified" as Subgroup AD, other preference eligibles "should be identified" as Subgroup A, and non-preference eligibles "should be identified" as Subgroup B. Final: "**must** be identified" in all three paragraphs.
25. **351.604 — proposed amendment dropped.** The proposed rule would have revised 351.604(b) and removed (d) (furloughs and recall by retention standing). The final rule contains no 351.604 amendment.
Q11.basis: 2026-04377, 91 FR 10926–10934 (amendatory instructions 17–38); 2026-15665, 91 FR 49218–49227 (amendatory instructions 17–37); 2026-17335, 91 FR 54794 (corrected list structure in 351.702(a)(4)(iv)).
Q11.uncertainty: Purely typographical differences are excluded per the question (for example "agency's'" to "agency's" in 351.503(c)(4); "all other employees in the occupying a career position" to "all other employees occupying a career position" in 351.502(b)(3); and the "430.208(d)" to "430.208(e)" renumbering). Items 12 and 16 are included because they change which section or subpart the operative reference points to, which is substantive for 351.505(b)(2) in particular; a reviewer applying a narrower reading of "citation format" might omit them.

Q12.answer:
**(a) Retention register for the GS-13 level (competitive-service tenure group; notices received Oct. 5, 2026; four-year window Oct. 5, 2022–Oct. 5, 2026; no cutoff date).**
- **Alvarez** — career, subgroup I. Ratings 5 (11/15/2023), 5 (11/14/2024), 4 (11/13/2025): 7+7+5 = **19.0**; no preference, +0 (Subgroup B). **Total 19.0.**
- **Brandt** — career, subgroup I. Ratings 3 (11/15/2023), 4 (11/14/2024), 2 (11/13/2025): 3+5+0 = **8.0**; 30%+ compensable disability, **+5** (Subgroup AD). **Total 13.0.**
- **Chen** — career, subgroup I. The Level 2 received **Sept. 30, 2022 is outside** the four-year window, so only two ratings count: Level 5 (11/14/2024) and Level 4 (11/13/2025). Proxy = (7+5)/2 = **6** (351.503(f)(2)); credit = 7+5+6 = **18.0**; no preference, +0. **Total 18.0.**
- **Dube** — career-conditional with the initial probationary period completed, so **subgroup II** (351.502(a)(3)). Two ratings, Level 4 (11/14/2024) and Level 4 (11/13/2025): proxy = (5+5)/2 = 5; credit = 5+5+5 = **15.0**; preference eligible with no disability, **+3** (Subgroup A). **Total 18.0.**
- **Estrada** — career, subgroup I. The **Level 5 received Oct. 20, 2026 postdates the Oct. 5, 2026 notices** and cannot be used (351.503(c)(1): ratings received in the four years before issuance). In-window ratings 4 (11/15/2023), 3 (11/14/2024), 4 (11/13/2025): 5+3+5 = **13.0**; preference eligible with no disability, **+3**. **Total 16.0.**
- **Farouk** — career, subgroup I. One actual rating, Level 3 (11/14/2024): 3 x 3 = **9.0** (351.503(f)(3)); no preference, +0. **Total 9.0.** He is also a **restoration protected employee**: restored July 13, 2026 after 14 months of uniformed service, so he remains within the one-year post-reemployment protection of 353.209(b) (351.203; 351.606(a)).
- **Quinn** — career-conditional, appointed March 2, 2026, still serving the initial probationary period, so **not a competing employee** (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); she is **not on the register** and may be retained while a competing employee is released (351.202(d)(3)).

**Order of retention:** 1 **Alvarez 19.0** (I); 2 **Chen 18.0** (I); 3 **Dube 18.0** (II); 4 **Estrada 16.0** (I); 5 **Brandt 13.0** (I); 6 **Farouk 9.0** (I). The tie at 18.0 is broken by tenure subgroup, subgroup I ahead of II (351.501(c)), so Chen is ahead of Dube; no SCD tie-break is needed.

**(b) Released: Brandt, Estrada and Dube.** From the bottom: Farouk (9.0), then Brandt (13.0), then Estrada (16.0), then Dube (18.0, subgroup II). Farouk, however, is a restoration protected employee: under 351.606(a)(2) the agency "may not release a restoration protected employee from his or her competitive level before the expiration of the applicable retention protection period if another competing employee may be released instead" (his protection runs to July 13, 2027). The agency must therefore pass over Farouk and release the next three: **Brandt, Estrada and Dube**. Alvarez, Chen and Farouk are retained; Quinn is not a competing employee. The record must document Farouk's ordinary standing, the basis and expiry of the protection, and each employee released because he was passed over (351.606(a)(6)).

**(c) Required offers (351.701(a)–(b)), comparing each holder's total, then subgroup, then SCD.**
- **Brandt (13.0; Subgroup AD; 30%+ disability, so the five-grade limit applies).** Lower-standing holders: only **Ikeda (9.0)**. Gomez (17.0), Hill (14.0) and Jones (15.0) all have higher retention standing than Brandt's 13.0, so 351.701(b)(1) bars those positions; GS-9 is four grades below GS-13 but within the five-grade limit. **Must be offered: Ikeda's GS-9.**
- **Estrada (16.0; no disability, so the three-grade limit applies: GS-12/11/10).** Lower-standing holders: Hill (14.0), Jones (15.0) and Ikeda (9.0); **Gomez (17.0) is higher**, so the GS-12 is unavailable, and GS-9 is outside the three-grade limit. Between GS-11 (Hill) and GS-10 (Jones), the rule requires "no reduction, or the least possible reduction, in representative rate," so **must be offered: Hill's GS-11.**
- **Dube (18.0; subgroup II; no disability, so the three-grade limit applies).** Dube's 18.0 exceeds every holder's total (Gomez 17.0, Jones 15.0, Hill 14.0, Ikeda 9.0); the tenure subgroup matters only as a tie-breaker (351.501(c)), so all four have lower retention standing. GS-9 is outside the limit; the least possible reduction is at GS-12, so **must be offered: Gomez's GS-12.**

**(d) If every offer is accepted: Gomez, Hill and Ikeda are separated.** Brandt moves into the GS-9, Estrada into the GS-11 and Dube into the GS-12 (each retaining the same status and tenure, 351.701(a)). The three displaced incumbents are released from their competitive levels, and the scenario states they are qualified only for the position they hold, so they have no assignment rights and are separated. Alvarez, Chen and Farouk remain in GS-13 positions, Quinn remains (not a competing employee), and Jones remains in the GS-10. **The employees separated from the agency are Gomez, Hill and Ikeda.**
Q12.basis: 5 CFR 351.202(d), 351.203 ("initial probationary period," "restoration protected employee"), 351.501–351.507, 351.601(c), 351.606(a)(1)–(6), 351.701(a)–(b), as revised by 2026-15665 (91 FR 49218–49226); 5 CFR 353.209(b), as revised at 91 FR 49226.
Q12.uncertainty: Two points are not fully resolved by the text. (1) Farouk's one-year (rather than six-month) protection period rests on 38 U.S.C. 4316(c) as described in the preamble (91 FR 49202: one year where the uniformed service exceeded 180 days), not on text printed in the rule. (2) 351.606(a)(2) directs the agency to pass over a protected employee if another competing employee may be released instead, but neither 351.606 nor 351.701 addresses two released employees with rights to the same position; on these facts the three rights attach to three different positions, so the issue does not arise.

Q13.answer:
Places where the preamble of 2026-15665 differs from the amendatory instructions or regulatory text printed in the same document:

1. **Erosion-of-duties reclassification: wrong paragraph and an extra "180 days" trigger.** Preamble (91 FR 49190): "OPM is modifying **Sec. 351.201(a)(2)** to remove from the list of actions that require agencies to use RIF procedures reclassification of an employee's position due to erosion of duties if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF ... **and the RIF would take effect within 180 days**." The text: 351.201(a)(2) as revised (91 FR 49218) contains no erosion-of-duties language at all; the operative provision is **351.202(c)(3)** (91 FR 49218), which bars the reclassification "between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force in the employee's competitive area and the completion of the reduction in force where the reclassification action would adversely affect an employee's retention standing" — **no 180-day element**. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49190 ("this rule will bar agencies from undertaking an erosion-of-duties reclassification between the formal announcement and completion of a RIF if the action would adversely affect an employee's retention standing").

2. **Competitive-area submission: "for OPM review" vs "approval in advance."** Preamble (91 FR 49179, summary of changes from the proposal): "an agency must submit a description of the competitive area and provide, **for OPM review**, a written explanation of the bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area." Regulatory text, 351.402(c) (91 FR 49220): the agency "shall submit a description of the competitive area, along with a written statement explaining the bona fide organizational basis for the competitive area, **to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force**." **Another passage is correct:** 91 FR 49203 ("the requirement in Sec. 351.402(c) that OPM **approve** new or substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less than 90 days prior to the issuance of RIF notices").

3. **Employees excluded "without using RIF procedures" vs a required modified notice.** Executive Summary (91 FR 49178): employees serving initial probationary periods, trial periods, temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less, and Schedule C/G employees "are not 'competing employees' for RIF purposes and can be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted, or reassigned **without using RIF procedures**." Regulatory text, 351.202(d)(4) (91 FR 49218): if such an employee is furloughed for more than 30 days, separated, demoted or reassigned for a 351.201(a)(2) reason (and the action is not merely the expiration of a temporary or time-limited appointment), "the agency **must provide written notice under Sec. 351.801**," including specified content and a statement that the employee is not a competing employee and was not ranked. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49179 (summary item 4) and 91 FR 49190–49191 ("the revised text clarifies that these excluded employees are still subject to the notice provisions of Sec. 351.801").

4. **Tenure subgroup II: "temporary or term appointment" vs "temporary appointment ... under subpart D."** Preamble (91 FR 49196): "Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other competitive service employee who, as of the date of the RIF notice, is not serving an initial probationary period or a **temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less**"; the preceding paragraph (91 FR 49196) says the tenure group excludes those serving "an initial probationary period or a **temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR part 316**." Regulatory text, 351.502(a)(3) (91 FR 49220): subgroup II includes employees not in subgroup I who are "not serving an initial probationary period or a **temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316**" — no term appointments, no time-limited appointments, and only subpart D. **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49190 ("a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of 5 CFR part 316") and 91 FR 49190–49191 (the final rule "removes a proposed reference to term appointments under part 316 subpart C").

5. **Missing ratings: where the "modal rating" comes from.** Preamble (91 FR 49198): paragraph (f) of 351.503 "uses the modal rating concept for employees with no ratings during the 4-year period prior to the RIF, **as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)**." Regulatory text, 351.503(f)(1) (91 FR 49221): credit "must be based on the modal rating **as defined in Sec. 351.203** for the summary level pattern that applies...." The two passages point to different sources, and the amendatory instructions add no "modal rating" definition to 351.203. A later passage (91 FR 49203) refers only to "use of the modal rating," citing neither, so the preamble nowhere states the point consistently with the text.

6. **Use of ratings: "may be considered" vs "must be based on."** Preamble (91 FR 49197): "Generally, the three most recent ratings of record received during the 4-year period prior to the date of issuance of reduction in force notices **may be considered**; however, an agency may establish a cut-off date...." Regulatory text, 351.503(c)(1) (91 FR 49220): "A competing employee's entitlement to performance consideration under this subpart **must be based on** the employee's three most recent summary level ratings of record received during the 4-year period...." **Another passage states it correctly:** 91 FR 49197 ("Agencies will list competing employees on the retention register ... based on each employee's performance credit, which is the sum of the values assigned for their three most recent ratings of record").
Q13.uncertainty: Whether item 6 is a true conflict depends on reading "entitlement ... must be based on" as mandatory; the preamble's "may be considered" may be describing the discretion to adopt a cutoff date rather than the use of ratings. Items 1 and 2 are contradictions in substance; item 5 is a cross-reference conflict that cannot be resolved because 351.203's definition of "modal rating" is not printed.

Q14.answer:
**A. (i) Preamble statements in OPM's appeals rule that differ from its regulatory text (as published or as corrected).**

1. **"Part 351" vs "this subpart."** The preamble says the final text provides that **part 351 procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action** — 91 FR 49230 (digest, "Revising exclusivity language"), 91 FR 49243 ("Final Sec. 351.901(c) states that the procedures in **part 351** are the sole and exclusive means"), 91 FR 49244, 91 FR 49248 ("Paragraph (c)(1) provides that the procedures in **part 351** are the sole and exclusive means"), and 91 FR 49257. As **published**, the text read "The procedures in **this part** are the sole and exclusive means ..." (91 FR 49263), matching the preamble; the **correction** changed it to "The procedures in **this subpart** are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a reduction-in-force action taken under this part" (2026-17338, 91 FR 54796, item 1). The preamble was not conformed, so as corrected the rule's exclusivity reaches only subpart I procedures, while the preamble describes part 351 as the exclusive vehicle.

2. **Burden of proof: "timely and in the required form" vs "timeliness."** Preamble (91 FR 49248): "The appellant must prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the written appeal was **timely and in the required form**; that OPM has jurisdiction ...; that the agency failed to comply ...; and that the failure prejudiced the appellant." Regulatory text, 351.901(b)(1) (91 FR 49263, unchanged by the correction), requires proof only of "[t]he **timeliness** of the written appeal." The text contains no required-form element (form and content appear in 351.903 without a burden allocation), and no other preamble passage states the burden without it.

3. **The undefined term in 351.904(c).** Preamble (91 FR 49231): "**OPM or the responsible agency** may disallow an employee's choice of representative only where the representative is an employee of the responsible agency or OPM...." Text as corrected (2026-17338, 91 FR 54796, item 3): "**OPM or the agency whose action is under appeal** may ... disallow an employee's choice of representative when the representative is an employee of **that agency** or OPM...." OPM's correction notes that "responsible agency" is "undefined in part 351."

**B. (ii) Changes from the proposed appeals rule to the final rule that the final rule's summary of changes from the proposal does not acknowledge** (summary at 91 FR 49230–49232; proposed text at 91 FR 5874–5877).

1. **FLRA removed from the list of preserved forums.** Proposed 351.901(c) (91 FR 5874): the exclusive procedure does not preclude a complaint, appeal or other matter within the jurisdiction of EEOC, **the Federal Labor Relations Authority**, an Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS, or OSC. Final 351.901(c)(3) (91 FR 49263–49264): the list is EEOC, an Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS, and OSC — **FLRA is gone**, and a new bar on grievance procedures and arbitration appears instead. The digest's "Revising exclusivity language" paragraph (91 FR 49230) describes the grievance bar and the preserved forums but never flags the removal of FLRA.
2. **New exemption route in the e-filing registration requirement.** Proposed 351.902(c)(2) (91 FR 5875): "No party may electronically file any document with OPM or access an appeal or reconsideration of an appeal unless registered as an e-filer." Final 351.902(c)(2) (91 FR 49264): "... unless registered as an e-filer **or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause**." The digest's e-filing paragraphs (91 FR 49230–49231) discuss narrowed enforcement and the withdrawal rule but not this carve-out.
3. **Hearing provision narrowed; "any other appropriate action" dropped.** Proposed 351.905(c) (91 FR 5876): review is record-based "unless OPM determines that a hearing **or any other appropriate action** is necessary and efficient to resolve an appeal **and directs the parties to participate in such hearing or comply with such action**." Final 351.905(c) (91 FR 49265): "... unless OPM determines that a **hearing** is necessary and efficient in resolving an appeal." The digest (91 FR 49231, "Tightening audits and investigations") addresses the audit/investigation standard but not the deletion of "any other appropriate action" or of the direction to the parties.
4. **Sanctions made discretionary.** Proposed 351.906(b) (91 FR 5876): when a party fails to comply with a directive, OPM "**shall**, except when prohibited by law," draw adverse inferences, prohibit evidence, or eliminate submissions. Final 351.906(b) (91 FR 49266): OPM "**may**, except when prohibited by law: ...." The digest's "Refining protective-order authority" paragraph (91 FR 49231) does not mention the change from "shall" to "may."
5. **New proportionality limit on sanctions.** Final 351.906(c) (91 FR 49266) adds: "Any sanction issued under paragraph (b) of this section must be proportionate, causally related to the violation, and no broader than necessary to protect the adjudicatory process." The proposed rule had no such paragraph and the digest does not acknowledge its addition.

**C. (iii) Inconsistencies about which RIF appeals the Board will still hear.**

1. **Within MSPB's rule: "action taken"/ "notice issued" vs "RIF effective date."** MSPB's DATES (91 FR 51997) say it "will not apply this rule to pending cases or to newly filed cases relating to **agency actions taken before the effective date** of OPM's rulemakings, and will continue to adjudicate such ... RIF appeals"; and its text (91 FR 51997) says MSPB "will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals that are not covered by OPM's final RIF appeals rule (i.e., because the RIF actions were taken before the rule's effective date), and will accept such cases for filing **where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date**." But Section III, "Effective Date of Amendment" (91 FR 51998), says: "MSPB will adjudicate **any RIF appeals it receives after September 2, 2026, in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026**." Three different triggers — date the action was taken, date the RIF notice was issued, and the RIF's own effective date — yield different answers whenever a notice issues before Sept. 2 but the separation takes effect after it (as in Q7(a): notice Aug. 31, 2026, separation Oct. 30, 2026).
2. **Between the Board and OPM: the operative trigger.** OPM's rule turns on the **date the agency issues the specific RIF notice**: it "applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026" (2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230; preamble 91 FR 49262). MSPB's Section III turns on the **RIF effective date**, so for the same employee the Board's Section III and OPM's DATES can point in opposite directions.
3. **Between the Board and OPM: retained jurisdiction vs OPM's exclusivity claim.** OPM's preamble calls part 351 the "sole and exclusive means" of appealing a RIF action (91 FR 49230, 49243, 49244, 49248, 49257) and the corrected text calls subpart I that means (91 FR 54796), while MSPB expressly **retains** RIF appeal jurisdiction for one category — Foreign Service RIF actions under 22 U.S.C. 4010a — in redesignated 5 CFR 1201.3(a)(5) (91 FR 51998). OPM's 351.901(c)(3) preserves matters within the independent jurisdiction of MSPB (91 FR 49264), which reconciles the two; but the OPM text contains **no applicability limitation at all** (OPM says so at 91 FR 49248: "the final regulatory text accordingly does not include a separate applicability note in Sec. 351.901"), so an employee whose notice issued Aug. 31, 2026 is directed by OPM's preamble to MSPB and by MSPB's Section III (if the separation took effect after Sept. 2) elsewhere.
Q14.uncertainty: Item A.1 depends on the correction: before the Sept. 2, 2026 effective date the preamble and the text agreed (both "this part"), and after the correction the preamble is out of step. Item A.3 is a terminology difference that OPM itself described as non-substantive. For part C, the Board's three formulations cannot all be applied at once, and neither the Board's rule nor OPM's states a tie-breaking rule; how MSPB will docket a case with a pre-Sept. 2 notice and a post-Sept. 2 effective date is not resolved by the documents.
